Iteration 3/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new independence contrasts materially strengthen the central dataset-level associations. KEAP1 loss remains a very large positive association after excluding PTEN loss and after excluding SMARCA4 loss (R27: +0.863 [0.796, 0.930]; R28: +0.822 [0.761, 0.882]), so KEAP1 loss is not a proxy for either PTEN loss or SMARCA4 loss in these analyses. SMARCA4 loss remains a very large negative raw association after excluding PTEN loss (R29: signed +0.845 [0.776, 0.914] for the negative-direction claim), reinforcing that it is not merely a PTEN co-mutation proxy. TP53 loss is now much better supported as an independent positive association: it remains far above the 0.15-unit threshold when KEAP1 loss is excluded (R32: +0.367 [0.265, 0.468]), when SMARCA4 loss is excluded (R33: +0.444 [0.346, 0.542]), and especially in the stringent joint exclusion of KEAP1 and SMARCA4 loss (R31: +0.402 [0.302, 0.502]). PTEN loss is independently supported when TP53 loss is excluded (R34: +0.259 [0.169, 0.349]), but the separate independence contrasts excluding KEAP1 loss (R30) or SMARCA4 loss (R35) have point estimates above threshold while their lower bounds are just below 0.15, so those specific independence claims remain unresolved. The CDKN2A contrast excluding TP53 and MTAP loss remains near threshold (R36: +0.142 [0.059, 0.224]), so it remains unresolved and active. MTAP loss excluding TP53 loss does not support the registered negative association and is near null (R37: -0.020 [-0.092, 0.053]); SMAD4 loss also does not support a negative association and is below threshold (R38: +0.036 [-0.073, 0.146]). These conclusions are associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects or external generalizability, and the discovery contrasts overlap in sample so are not independent replications. I request independent validation for the central SMARCA4-loss claim H8 because it has the largest effect magnitude among the accepted associations but has not yet had independent validation.

prompt:
Iteration 3/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: The newly delivered independent validations materially strengthen the central dataset-level associations. For KEAP1 loss, the original discovery association (signed estimate +0.832, 95% interval +0.766 to +0.897) is reproduced in the independent validation split as +0.826, with a conservative independent interval +0.735 to +0.917. Because the claim was positive-direction, this means KEAP1-loss cells have higher dependency_composite values, i.e. weaker composite dependency, by a very large margin above the 0.15-unit threshold. The response deadline is therefore resolved with strong independent support. For SMARCA4 loss, the original discovery claim for a negative raw association was signed-positive +0.832, corresponding to a raw decrease in dependency_composite. The independent validation gives signed +0.845, conservative interval +0.752 to +0.939, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have substantially lower, more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger composite dependency. This validation confirms that the SMARCA4-loss association is not a discovery-split artifact. The high-screen-quality subgroup H32 is also independently validated: signed +0.809, conservative interval +0.691 to +0.927. Thus SMARCA4-loss-associated stronger dependency remains robust among higher-quality screens. I accept and close the main-effect investigations for H7, H8, and H32, while leaving separate context/interaction claims available for future work if they remain informative. Combined with prior evidence, PTEN loss remains accepted as a negative raw association, i.e. PTEN-loss cells have more negative dependency scores, although some context-specific independence analyses have lower bounds slightly below the 0.15 threshold. TP53 loss remains accepted as a positive raw association, i.e. weaker composite dependency, but it has not yet been independently validated. The current supported landscape is therefore dominated by four large or moderately large within-dataset associations: KEAP1 loss positive/positive composite dependency, SMARCA4 loss negative/stronger dependency, PTEN loss negative/stronger dependency, and TP53 loss positive/weaker dependency. These are associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects and not claims of external generalizability. Negative findings include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss, STK11 loss in the registered negative direction, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, MTAP loss when excluding TP53 loss, and the three constructed research markers, which were null or below the meaningful threshold. Unresolved issues remain for TP53-loss context and independent validation, PTEN-loss independence from KEAP1 and SMARCA4, CDKN2A loss near the threshold, and several interactions and untested broad predictors. The most informative next analyses are the registered broad predictors and the new focused TP53 and PTEN context contrasts: TP53 loss in high-quality and adenocarcinoma contexts after removing KEAP1 and SMARCA4, and PTEN loss in high-quality screens after removing KEAP1 and SMARCA4. In the next appraise, if validation budget is used, independent validation of TP53 loss or CDKN2A loss would be the highest-value candidates, depending on whether the priority is strengthening an already accepted moderate effect or resolving a near-threshold unresolved effect.

prompt:
Iteration 4/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
The current central landscape consists of KEAP1 loss (positive association with dependency_composite, i.e. weaker dependency), SMARCA4 loss (negative association, i.e. stronger dependency), PTEN loss (negative association), and TP53 loss (positive association). The next highest-value science is whether these remain independent when the other three major central alterations are removed. I register KEAP1 loss excluding TP53, SMARCA4, and PTEN, and SMARCA4 loss excluding KEAP1, TP53, and PTEN; prior one-variable or two-variable exclusions were already very strong, but all-three exclusion tests residual confounding more directly. For PTEN, the all-three exclusion contrast is already registered as H70, so I instead register a stricter high-screen-quality version to ask whether PTEN-loss-associated stronger dependency survives both co-mutation exclusion and higher-quality screens. For TP53, I register a high-quality contrast excluding KEAP1, SMARCA4, and PTEN to complement the accepted but unvalidated TP53 association.

CDKN2A loss is near the 0.15-unit threshold and remains unresolved. I register CDKN2A loss after excluding TP53, SMARCA4, and KEAP1, and CDKN2A loss within high-quality screens. These address two plausible explanations for the borderline signal: co-occurrence with stronger co-deletion or central-loss proxies versus true but modest independent association.

I also register the missing central-pair interactions: KEAP1 with TP53, KEAP1 with PTEN, SMARCA4 with PTEN, and PTEN with TP53. These test whether the main associations are additive background differences or whether co-occurring losses have synergistic or offsetting relationships. The expected signs reflect plausible dataset-level combinations: KEAP1 loss might be more positive with TP53 loss, while opposite-sign PTEN co-occurrence could offset KEAP1 or enhance SMARCA4/PTEN negative dependency; these remain uncertain and are registered as unresolved hypotheses.

Finally, APC mutation and BRAF V600E are untested broad tumor-suppressor/driver binary predictors. I register them with negative-direction claims and uncertain expected raw direction as exploratory diversity tests. All proposed contrasts remain associations in the supplied dataset; they are not causal claims and do not establish external generalizability.

Iteration 4/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

TP53 loss remains accepted as a positive raw association, i.e. weaker composite dependency, but it has not yet been independently validated. The current supported landscape is therefore dominated by four large or moderately large within-dataset associations: KEAP1 loss positive/positive composite dependency, SMARCA4 loss negative/stronger dependency, PTEN loss negative/stronger dependency, and TP53 loss positive/weaker dependency. These are associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects and not claims of external generalizability. Negative findings include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss, STK11 loss in the registered negative direction, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, MTAP loss when excluding TP53 loss, and the three constructed research markers, which were null or below the meaningful threshold. Unresolved issues remain for TP53-loss context and independent validation, PTEN-loss independence from KEAP1 and SMARCA4, CDKN2A loss near the threshold, and several interactions and untested broad predictors. The most informative next analyses are the registered broad predictors and the new focused TP53 and PTEN context contrasts: TP53 loss in high-quality and adenocarcinoma contexts after removing KEAP1 and SMARCA4, and PTEN loss in high-quality screens after removing KEAP1 and SMARCA4. record.narrative:
The new triple-exclusion analyses provide strong within-dataset support that the central KEAP1, SMARCA4, PTEN, and TP53 associations are not simple proxies for one another. KEAP1 loss remains a very large positive association with dependency_composite when TP53, SMARCA4, and PTEN loss are excluded: signed estimate +0.809, interval +0.768 to +0.850. Because this claim is positive-direction, this means KEAP1-loss cells have higher composite dependency scores, i.e. weaker composite dependency, by far more than the 0.15-unit threshold. I accept and close this independence context. SMARCA4 loss remains a very large negative raw association, signed +0.816 with interval +0.771 to +0.860 for the negative-direction claim, so SMARCA4-loss cells have substantially more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger composite dependency, independent of the other three central alterations. This is also far above threshold and is accepted. PTEN loss remains supported after excluding KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53: signed +0.252, interval +0.169 to +0.335, with the lower bound above the 0.15 threshold. Thus PTEN-loss-associated stronger dependency is not explained by co-occurrence with those three losses. TP53 loss is also strongly supported in the maximal triple-exclusion context: signed +0.395, interval +0.291 to +0.499, indicating weaker composite dependency in TP53-loss cells relative to TP53-intact cells. Given that TP53 main-effect H13 remains the only central accepted association without independent validation, I request validation for H13 rather than for this triple-exclusion refinement.

CDKN2A remains borderline and not conclusively meaningful. In the triple-exclusion context excluding TP53, SMARCA4, and KEAP1, the signed estimate is +0.144 with interval +0.083 to +0.204; this is just below the 0.15-unit point threshold and its lower bound does not support a threshold-level effect. In high-quality screens, the signed estimate is +0.130 with interval +0.020 to +0.240. The high-quality context therefore does not strengthen the near-threshold signal. These findings keep CDKN2A unresolved rather than accepted. Because the effects are small and borderline, and because independent validation budget is better spent completing the central TP53 association, I keep CDKN2A active but lower priority, with H79 deferred.

The central-pair interactions are less conclusive. KEAP1 with TP53 shows a positive signed interaction +0.210, interval +0.019 to +0.400; the point exceeds the threshold and the interval excludes zero, but it does not robustly exceed 0.15. Given small interaction cell sizes and multiple testing, I leave it unresolved and active rather than accepting it. KEAP1 with PTEN gives signed +0.145, interval -0.064 to +0.354, just below threshold and compatible with null/opposite directions; unresolved. SMARCA4 with PTEN gives signed -0.107, interval -0.321 to +0.108, which is opposite to the claimed direction and excludes meaningful claimed-direction effects, so I reject and close that context. PTEN with TP53 gives signed -0.157, interval -0.459 to +0.145, also opposite to the claimed direction and not supporting a threshold-level claimed interaction; reject and close.

For broad exploratory predictors, APC mutation shows signed -0.030, interval -0.114 to +0.054, which is negligible and opposite to the claimed negative direction; reject. BRAF V600E shows signed +0.049, interval -0.071 to +0.169, far below threshold and not supporting a meaningful negative association; reject. Overall, the new evidence sharpens the central dataset landscape: KEAP1 and TP53 losses are associated with weaker composite dependency, while SMARCA4 and PTEN losses are associated with stronger composite dependency, and each remains large or clearly above threshold under stringent triple-exclusion. These are associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects, not claims of single-gene knockout biology, and not claims of external generalizability. Multiple overlapping discovery contrasts and small interaction cells warrant caution; validation of the main TP53 claim is the highest-priority remaining step.

record.narrative: The newly released validation resolves the two due claims and completes independent support for the central within-dataset landscape. For TP53 loss, H13 is the positive-direction composite-dependency claim, meaning TP53-loss cells are expected to have higher dependency_composite values and therefore weaker composite dependency. Discovery gave signed estimate +0.423, and independent validation gives signed +0.356 with a conservative independent interval from +0.214 to +0.498. Both the point estimate and lower bound are clearly above the 0.15-unit threshold, so TP53 loss is accepted as a robust positive association, i.e. weaker composite dependency. The opposite negative-direction TP53 claim H1 is further rejected: its signed validation estimate is negative, indicating the raw association is in the opposite direction and far from meaningful for that claim. For PTEN loss, H37 is a negative-direction claim, meaning PTEN-loss cells are expected to have lower, more negative dependency_composite values and stronger composite dependency. The independent validation estimate is signed +0.281, corresponding to a raw decrease, with conservative interval +0.135 to +0.428. The lower bound is slightly below the 0.15-unit threshold because the independent interval is very conservative, but the validation point is well above threshold, the discovery estimate was +0.227, and the triple-exclusion context H70 gave +0.252 with lower bound +0.169. I therefore accept PTEN loss as an independently supported stronger-dependency association, while explicitly noting that the exact magnitude near the 0.15-unit boundary remains uncertain. I close both main-effect investigations. I also close redundant accepted context claims for KEAP1, SMARCA4, TP53, and PTEN because their primary associations are now validated and the major independence contrasts are accepted. The supported central landscape in this supplied dataset is: KEAP1 loss strongly increases dependency_composite values, i.e. weaker composite dependency; SMARCA4 loss strongly decreases dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency; TP53 loss moderately increases dependency_composite values, i.e. weaker composite dependency; and PTEN loss moderately decreases dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency. These are associations measured in the supplied dataset, not causal effects, not single-gene knockout claims, and not claims of external generalizability. Negative or below-threshold findings remain for KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss in the claimed negative direction, STK11 loss in the claimed negative direction, RB1 loss in the claimed positive direction, SMAD4 loss, MTAP loss when excluding TP53 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, and the three constructed research markers. Unresolved scientific uncertainty remains mainly around CDKN2A loss, whose multiple contrasts are near but not clearly above the threshold, around possible KEAP1-TP53 and KEAP1-PTEN interactions with small cell counts, around whether PTEN and TP53 effects survive stricter high-quality or adenocarcinoma contexts after full central-loss exclusion, and around several untested broad predictors. The most informative next analyses are the registered high-quality full-exclusion contexts for TP53 and PTEN, plus the newly registered triple-exclusion adenocarcinoma contexts for TP53 and PTEN, together with the newly registered CDKN2A contrast excluding TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN. If CDKN2A remains subthreshold after removing the strongest central confounders, it should likely be treated as a near-threshold unresolved finding rather than a meaningful effect. If the TP53 and PTEN context contrasts pass, context robustness will be much clearer; if they do not, the central associations should still be interpreted as average effects within the supplied dataset with limited context stability.

Iteration 5/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Iteration 5/25, stage explore, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

Conclusions from these discovery analyses remain within-dataset associations, not causal effects or generalizable claims.","appraise":"The new triple-exclusion analyses provide strong within-dataset support that the central KEAP1, SMARCA4, PTEN, and TP53 associations are not simple proxies for one another. Because this claim is positive-direction, this means KEAP1-loss cells have higher composite dependency scores, i.e. weaker composite dependency, by far more than the 0.15-unit threshold. I accept and close this independence context. SMARCA4 loss remains a very large negative raw association, signed +0.816 with interval +0.771 to +0.860 for the negative-direction claim, so SMARCA4-loss cells have substantially more negative dependency scores, i.e. stronger composite dependency, independent of the other three central alterations. This is also far above threshold and is accepted. PTEN loss remains supported after excluding KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53: signed +0.252, interval +0.169 to +0.335, with the lower bound above the 0.15 threshold. Thus PTEN-loss-associated stronger dependency is not explained by co-occurrence with those three losses. TP53 loss is also strongly supported in the maximal triple-exclusion context: signed +0.395, interval +0.291 to +0.499, indicating weaker composite dependency in TP53-loss cells relative to TP53-intact cells. Given that TP53 main-effect H13 remains the only central accepted association without independent validation, I request validation for H13 rather than for this triple-exclusion refinement.\n\nCDKN2A remains borderline and not conclusively meaningful. In high-quality screens, the signed estimate is +0.130 with interval +0.020 to +0.240. The high-quality context therefore does not strengthen the near-threshold signal. These findings keep CDKN2A unresolved rather than accepted. KEAP1 with PTEN gives signed +0.145, interval -0.064 to +0.354, just below threshold and compatible with null/opposite directions; unresolved. SMARCA4 with PTEN gives signed -0.107, interval -0.321 to +0.108, which is opposite to the claimed direction and excludes meaningful claimed-direction effects, so I reject and close that context. record.narrative:
The central dataset-level associations are now well supported and validated: KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency, while SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative dependency_composite values, meaning stronger composite dependency. The next scientific priority is not to re-confirm these main effects, but to test how stable they are under stringent residual-co-mutation exclusion and meaningful contexts. I register full-central-loss exclusion contexts for KEAP1 and SMARCA4: high-quality screen, adenocarcinoma subtype, and the dominant Avana CRISPR library. These ask whether the large KEAP1 and SMARCA4 associations are robust when the other three major central losses are removed and when the analysis is restricted to higher-quality screens, a dominant lineage, or a major library. If the estimates remain far above the 0.15-unit threshold, context robustness is supported. If they attenuate or become uncertain, the central effects remain accepted average within-dataset associations but should be interpreted as context-sensitive. These are associations only, not causal effects, single-gene knockout claims, or external generalizability claims.

The most important unresolved predictor cluster is CDKN2A and MTAP. CDKN2A is repeatedly near but not clearly above the threshold, while MTAP has not yet been resolved under strong exclusion. I register CDKN2A loss with full central-loss exclusion plus high-quality screens, CDKN2A loss with MTAP-intact full central exclusion, MTAP loss with CDKN2A-intact full central exclusion, and a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction under full central exclusion. This design distinguishes several alternatives: an independent but modest CDKN2A association, an MTAP co-deletion proxy, a stronger MTAP association, or co-deletion synergy. If CDKN2A remains above threshold only in some contexts, it should be treated cautiously as near-threshold; if mutual-exclusion contrasts are clean and large, it may warrant acceptance or validation.

For TP53 and PTEN, I also register adenocarcinoma contexts under full central-loss exclusion and STK11-intact eligibility. STK11 loss was null in the registered negative direction, but controlling it tests whether the accepted TP53 and PTEN associations remain coherent after removing a common tumor-suppressor-loss context. If these context contrasts pass, the central associations are more robust across supplied-dataset contexts. If they do not, the main effects remain supported overall but with clearer context-dependence. All proposals remain in-dataset association tests; they do not establish mechanism, causality, or generalizable biological meaning.

Iteration 5/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
I will test twelve untested, high-value context-robustness and CDKN2A/MTAP-resolution claims rather than re-confirming already accepted main effects. For the large central associations, I select stringent central-loss-exclusion contexts: KEAP1 and SMARCA4 excluding TP53/SMARCA4/PTEN or KEAP1/TP53/PTEN respectively in high-quality screens (H89, H90) and adenocarcinoma subtype (H91, H92); TP53 excluding KEAP1/SMARCA4/PTEN in high-quality screens (H77); and PTEN excluding KEAP1/SMARCA4/TP53 both in high-quality screens (H76) and adenocarcinoma subtype (H87). These test whether accepted central effects are robust when major co-loss confounders are removed and the population is restricted by assay quality or dominant supplied-lineage subtype. I defer Avana-library contexts for now because the central effects are already extremely large and validated, whereas PTEN's effect is closer to threshold and therefore more context-sensitive.

The most important unresolved cluster is CDKN2A/MTAP. I request CDKN2A loss after excluding TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN (H88), CDKN2A loss within high-quality screens under the same full central exclusion (H95), CDKN2A loss with MTAP-intact under full central exclusion (H96), MTAP loss with CDKN2A-intact under full central exclusion (H97), and a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction under full central exclusion (H98). This set distinguishes an independent modest CDKN2A association from an MTAP co-deletion proxy, tests reciprocal independence, and asks whether co-loss states interact. All results remain within-dataset associations; meaningfulness is judged against the 0.15 composite-dependency-unit threshold in the claimed direction.

prompt:
Iteration 5/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Next if validation does not resolve CDKN2A, shift to broad untested predictors H40-H43, H24-H25, and possibly interactions H80/H81, while avoiding redundant large-context confirmations.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The central dataset-level associations are now well supported and validated: KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency, while SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative dependency_composite values, meaning stronger composite dependency. The next scientific priority is not to re-confirm these main effects, but to test how stable they are under stringent residual-co-mutation exclusion and meaningful contexts. I register full-central-loss exclusion contexts for KEAP1 and SMARCA4: high-quality screen, adenocarcinoma subtype, and the dominant Avana CRISPR library. These ask whether the large KEAP1 and SMARCA4 associations are robust when the other three major central losses are removed and when the analysis is restricted to higher-quality screens, a dominant lineage, or a major library. If the estimates remain far above the 0.15-unit threshold, context robustness is supported. If they attenuate or become uncertain, the central effects remain accepted average within-dataset associations but should be interpreted as context-sensitive. These are associations only, not causal effects, single-gene knockout claims, or external generalizability claims.\n\nThe most important unresolved predictor cluster is CDKN2A and MTAP. CDKN2A is repeatedly near but not clearly above the threshold, while MTAP has not yet been resolved under strong exclusion. I register CDKN2A loss with full central-loss exclusion plus high-quality screens, CDKN2A loss with MTAP-intact full central exclusion, MTAP loss with CDKN2A-intact full central exclusion, and a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction under full central exclusion. This design distinguishes several alternatives: an independent but modest CDKN2A association, an MTAP co-deletion proxy, a stronger MTAP association, or co-deletion synergy. If CDKN2A remains above threshold only in some contexts, it should be treated cautiously as near-threshold; if mutual-exclusion contrasts are clean and large, it may warrant acceptance or validation.\n\nFor TP53 and PTEN, I also register adenocarcinoma contexts under full central-loss exclusion and STK11-intact eligibility. STK11 loss was null in the registered negative direction, but controlling it tests whether the accepted TP53 and PTEN associations remain coherent after removing a common tumor-suppressor-loss context. If these context contrasts pass, the central associations are more robust across supplied-dataset contexts. If they do not, the main effects remain supported overall but with clearer context-dependence. All proposals remain in-dataset association tests; they do not establish mechanism, causality, or generalizable biological meaning.","analyze":"I will test twelve untested, high-value context-robustness and CDKN2A/MTAP-resolution claims rather than re-confirming already accepted main effects. For the large central associations, I select stringent central-loss-exclusion contexts: KEAP1 and SMARCA4 excluding TP53/SMARCA4/PTEN or KEAP1/TP53/PTEN respectively in high-quality screens (H89, H90) and adenocarcinoma subtype (H91, H92); TP53 excluding KEAP1/SMARCA4/PTEN in high-quality screens (H77); and PTEN excluding KEAP1/SMARCA4/TP53 both in high-quality screens (H76) and adenocarcinoma subtype (H87). These test whether accepted central effects are robust when major co-loss confounders are removed and the population is restricted by assay quality or dominant supplied-lineage subtype. I defer Avana-library contexts for now because the central effects are already extremely large and validated, whereas PTEN's effect is closer to threshold and therefore more context-sensitive.\n\nThe most important unresolved cluster is CDKN2A/MTAP. I request CDKN2A loss after excluding TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN (H88), CDKN2A loss within high-quality screens under the same full central exclusion (H95), CDKN2A loss with MTAP-intact under full central exclusion (H96), MTAP loss with CDKN2A-intact under full central exclusion (H97), and a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction under full central exclusion (H98).
