record.narrative:
The two validation response deadlines are confirmatory and materially strengthen the SMARCA4 landscape. For the main SMARCA4-loss claim, independent validation gives a signed estimate of +0.845 with a conservative independent interval from +0.752 to +0.939. Because H8 is negative-direction, this means SMARCA4-loss cells have a lower, more negative dependency_composite value by far more than the 0.15-unit threshold. I therefore accept and close H8. The high-quality-screen SMARCA4 context also validates cleanly: signed estimate +0.809, interval +0.691 to +0.927. This is well above threshold, so H32 remains accepted and closed. These are within-dataset associations; the composite score is not a SMARCA4 knockout measurement and does not imply causal generalization.

The new validation for H88 changes the CDKN2A assessment. H88 asks whether CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger composite dependency by more than 0.15 after removing TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN loss. Discovery gave a signed estimate of +0.164 with a lower bound of +0.101. Independent validation, however, gives a smaller signed estimate of +0.121 with a conservative interval from +0.034 to +0.209. The validation direction is supportive, but the point estimate is below the threshold and the lower bound is far below it. Combined with the pattern of other CDKN2A contrasts being near but not threshold-robust, the best current conclusion is that CDKN2A loss may be weakly associated with stronger dependency, but the supplied dataset does not support a scientifically meaningful threshold-level independent association. I therefore leave the claim unresolved rather than falsely accepting it, but close it as low priority because current evidence argues that additional discovery-focused follow-up is unlikely to be more informative than completing broader predictor exploration.

I also close the redundant CDKN2A/MTAP follow-up investigations: main CDKN2A, TP53-intact CDKN2A, TP53/MTAP-intact CDKN2A, triple-exclusion CDKN2A, high-quality full-exclusion CDKN2A, MTAP-intact full-exclusion CDKN2A, and the CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction. MTAP itself remains much less supported: H97, MTAP loss after excluding the major central losses and CDKN2A, was opposite the claimed direction and far from threshold. Thus the data argue against a strong independent MTAP association or a large CDKN2A-MTAP synergy.

The central supported dataset landscape is now coherent and extensively tested: KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency; SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative dependency_composite values, meaning stronger composite dependency. KEAP1 and SMARCA4 remain extremely robust after stringent central-loss exclusion, high-quality screen restriction, and adenocarcinoma restriction. TP53 remains robust and independently validated. PTEN remains accepted from its main validated effect and strong central-loss-exclusion contexts, though the exact magnitude near the 0.15 threshold is less certain than for KEAP1 or SMARCA4. Negative or below-threshold findings include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss in the claimed negative direction, STK11 loss in the claimed negative direction, RB1 loss in the claimed positive direction, SMAD4 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, the three constructed research markers, and MTAP after central-loss exclusion. Remaining uncertainty is mainly confined to modest near-threshold CDKN2A signals, some low-powered interactions, and untested broad predictors such as ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, MSI-high, MTAP main effect, and technical/library indicators. The most informative next analyses are therefore to broaden beyond the central mutation set, starting with these untested binary predictors and technical indicators; if any pass threshold, focused follow-up or validation should be requested at the appraise stage. All conclusions remain association findings in the supplied dataset, not causal claims, single-gene knockout claims, or generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 6/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
The accepted central within-dataset landscape is now established: KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency, whereas SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative dependency_composite values, meaning stronger composite dependency. CDKN2A and MTAP are not accepted as meaningful independent associations. The next priority is therefore to broaden beyond the central mutation set rather than continue confirming already-supported effects. I register untested or focused contexts for biologically plausible secondary predictors: ERBB2 amplification in adenocarcinoma and in a central-loss-intact population, BRCA2 loss in a central-loss-intact population, NF1 loss in a central-loss-intact population, MSI-high in a central-loss-intact population, and MTAP loss with CDKN2A intact within high-quality screens. These tests ask whether secondary oncogenic or DNA-repair/immunophenotype features carry threshold-level associations, or whether previously observed near-threshold signals are simply context-limited. I expect ERBB2 amplification and BRCA2 loss to trend toward stronger composite dependency, but the directions are not fixed and could be attenuated after removing central confounders. NF1 and MSI-high are more uncertain, so the registered directions are primarily screens for meaningful offsets. MTAP with CDKN2A intact tests whether the prior null MTAP result after full exclusion was driven by co-deletion or low power.

I also register technical and environmental predictors that could induce threshold-level offsets in the composite score: media serum percentage, CRISPR library indicators, and omics availability. These are not biological mechanism hypotheses; they assess whether assay platform, culture condition, or data-availability context can shift dependency_composite by more than 0.15 units. Large offsets would not prove a biological effect and would instead indicate important context or measurement caution. The directions for technical predictors are mainly detection-oriented, with anticipated direction uncertain except where serum abundance could reasonably weaken measured dependency.

Finally, I register context-robustness and effect-modification proposals for the accepted central predictors using biologically or experimentally relevant continuous thresholds: high aneuploidy for PTEN loss, high mutation burden for TP53 loss, high hypoxia for KEAP1 loss, and fast growth rate for SMARCA4 loss. For each, I register both a within-subgroup mean difference and a formal interaction against the complement. This distinguishes a robust average effect that remains large in the subgroup from genuine effect modification in that context. These remain supplied-dataset associations only; they are not causal effects, not single-gene knockout claims, and not claims of external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 6/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Keep all conclusions as supplied-dataset associations only.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The accepted central within-dataset landscape is now established: KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency, whereas SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative dependency_composite values, meaning stronger composite dependency. CDKN2A and MTAP are not accepted as meaningful independent associations. The next priority is therefore to broaden beyond the central mutation set rather than continue confirming already-supported effects. I register untested or focused contexts for biologically plausible secondary predictors: ERBB2 amplification in adenocarcinoma and in a central-loss-intact population, BRCA2 loss in a central-loss-intact population, NF1 loss in a central-loss-intact population, MSI-high in a central-loss-intact population, and MTAP loss with CDKN2A intact within high-quality screens. These tests ask whether secondary oncogenic or DNA-repair/immunophenotype features carry threshold-level associations, or whether previously observed near-threshold signals are simply context-limited. I expect ERBB2 amplification and BRCA2 loss to trend toward stronger composite dependency, but the directions are not fixed and could be attenuated after removing central confounders. NF1 and MSI-high are more uncertain, so the registered directions are primarily screens for meaningful offsets. MTAP with CDKN2A intact tests whether the prior null MTAP result after full exclusion was driven by co-deletion or low power.\n\nI also register technical and environmental predictors that could induce threshold-level offsets in the composite score: media serum percentage, CRISPR library indicators, and omics availability. These are not biological mechanism hypotheses; they assess whether assay platform, culture condition, or data-availability context can shift dependency_composite by more than 0.15 units. Large offsets would not prove a biological effect and would instead indicate important context or measurement caution. The directions for technical predictors are mainly detection-oriented, with anticipated direction uncertain except where serum abundance could reasonably weaken measured dependency.\n\nFinally, I register context-robustness and effect-modification proposals for the accepted central predictors using biologically or experimentally relevant continuous thresholds: high aneuploidy for PTEN loss, high mutation burden for TP53 loss, high hypoxia for KEAP1 loss, and fast growth rate for SMARCA4 loss. For each, I register both a within-subgroup mean difference and a formal interaction against the complement. This distinguishes a robust average effect that remains large in the subgroup from genuine effect modification in that context. These remain supplied-dataset associations only; they are not causal effects, not single-gene knockout claims, and not claims of external generalizability.","analyze":"I will test twelve untested, high-value context-robustness and CDKN2A/MTAP-resolution claims rather than re-confirming already accepted main effects. For the large central associations, I select stringent central-loss-exclusion contexts: KEAP1 and SMARCA4 excluding TP53/SMARCA4/PTEN or KEAP1/TP53/PTEN respectively in high-quality screens (H89, H90) and adenocarcinoma subtype (H91, H92); TP53 excluding KEAP1/SMARCA4/PTEN in high-quality screens (H77); and PTEN excluding KEAP1/SMARCA4/TP53 both in high-quality screens (H76) and adenocarcinoma subtype (H87). These test whether accepted central effects are robust when major co-loss confounders are removed and the population is restricted by assay quality or dominant supplied-lineage subtype. I defer Avana-library contexts for now because the central effects are already extremely large and validated, whereas PTEN's effect is closer to threshold and therefore more context-sensitive.\n\nThe most important unresolved cluster is CDKN2A/MTAP. I request CDKN2A loss after excluding TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN (H88), CDKN2A loss within high-quality screens under the same full central exclusion (H95), CDKN2A loss with MTAP-intact under full central exclusion (H96), MTAP loss with CDKN2A-intact under full central exclusion (H97), and a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction under full central exclusion (H98). This set distinguishes an independent modest CDKN2A association from an MTAP co-deletion proxy, tests reciprocal independence, and asks whether co-loss states interact. All results remain within-dataset associations; meaningfulness is judged against the 0.15 composite-dependency-unit threshold in the claimed direction.","appraise":"These analyses test whether the accepted central associations are robust under stringent central-loss exclusion and important context restriction, and they resolve much of the CDKN2A/MTAP cluster. KEAP1 and SMARCA4 are very robust: under triple-exclusion plus high-quality screens, KEAP1 is signed +0.786 (interval +0.728 to +0.844) and SMARCA4 +0.817 (+0.761 to +0.874); under triple-exclusion plus adenocarcinoma, KEAP1 +0.803 (+0.752 to +0.854) and SMARCA4 +0.806 (+0.754 to +0.858). All are far above the 0.15-unit threshold, with large lower bounds. I accept and close H89-H92 as within-dataset context-robust associations: KEAP1-loss cells have higher composite scores (weaker dependency), and SMARCA4-loss cells have more negative scores (stronger dependency), not explained by the other three central losses.\n\nTP53 is similarly robust: triple-exclusion plus high-quality screens gives signed +0.433 (+0.301 to +0.566), far above threshold, so H77 is accepted and closed. PTEN shows a more moderate but coherent pattern: triple-exclusion plus adenocarcinoma gives +0.244 (+0.152 to +0.336), supporting acceptance of H87; triple-exclusion plus high-quality screens gives +0.229 but lower bound +0.126, below the threshold, so H76 is directionally supportive but not threshold-robust and is deferred. PTEN remains accepted overall from its validated main effect and robust triple-exclusion/adenocarcinoma context; the high-quality triple-exclusion context should be interpreted as compatible but imprecise.\n\nCDKN2A remains the key unresolved predictor. The strongest registered contrast to date is H88, CDKN2A loss after excluding TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN: signed +0.164, interval +0.101 to +0.228. This supports the claimed stronger-dependency direction and exceeds threshold at the point estimate, but its lower bound is below 0.15. Related CDKN2A contrasts are also near threshold: H95 high-quality full-exclusion +0.185 (+0.092 to +0.277), and H96 MTAP-intact full-exclusion +0.150 (+0.082 to +0.218). Together these suggest a possible modest independent CDKN2A association rather than a clear proxy artifact, but the evidence is not sufficiently threshold-robust to accept without independent confirmation. I therefore request validation for H88 and leave H88/H95/H96 unresolved pending that validation. H78 and H79 are deprioritized as redundant near-threshold discovery contexts.\n\nMTAP is much less supported. H97, MTAP loss after excluding TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, PTEN, and CDKN2A, gives signed -0.026 (-0.078 to +0.025), opposite to the claimed stronger-dependency direction and far from threshold; I reject and close it. The CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction under full central exclusion (H98) is +0.075 (-0.106 to +0.256), below threshold and underpowered with small cells; I leave it unresolved but deferred. These results argue against a strong independent MTAP effect or a large CDKN2A-MTAP co-deletion synergy in this dataset, while keeping open the possibility of a modest CDKN2A association. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects, single-gene knockout claims, or generalizable biological claims.","synthesize":"The two validation response deadlines are confirmatory and materially strengthen the SMARCA4 landscape. For the main SMARCA4-loss claim, independent validation gives a signed estimate of +0.845 with a conservative independent interval from +0.752 to +0.939. Because H8 is negative-direction, this means SMARCA4-loss cells have a lower, more negative dependency_composite value by far more than the 0.15-unit threshold. I therefore accept and close H8. The high-quality-screen SMARCA4 context also validates cleanly: signed estimate +0.809, interval +0.691 to +0.927. This is well above threshold, so H32 remains accepted and closed. These are within-dataset associations; the composite score is not a SMARCA4 knockout measurement and does not imply causal generalization.\n\nThe new validation for H88 changes the CDKN2A assessment. H88 asks whether CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger composite dependency by more than 0.15 after removing TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN loss. Discovery gave a signed estimate of +0.164 with a lower bound of +0.101. Independent validation, however, gives a smaller signed estimate of +0.121 with a conservative interval from +0.034 to +0.209. The validation direction is supportive, but the point estimate is below the threshold and the lower bound is far below it. Combined with the pattern of other CDKN2A contrasts being near but not threshold-robust, the best current conclusion is that CDKN2A loss may be weakly associated with stronger dependency, but the supplied dataset does not support a scientifically meaningful threshold-level independent association. I therefore leave the claim unresolved rather than falsely accepting it, but close it as low priority because current evidence argues that additional discovery-focused follow-up is unlikely to be more informative than completing broader predictor exploration.\n\nI also close the redundant CDKN2A/MTAP follow-up investigations: main CDKN2A, TP53-intact CDKN2A, TP53/MTAP-intact CDKN2A, triple-exclusion CDKN2A, high-quality full-exclusion CDKN2A, MTAP-intact full-exclusion CDKN2A, and the CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction. MTAP itself remains much less supported: H97, MTAP loss after excluding the major central losses and CDKN2A, was opposite the claimed direction and far from threshold. Thus the data argue against a strong independent MTAP association or a large CDKN2A-MTAP synergy.\n\nThe central supported dataset landscape is now coherent and extensively tested: KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency; SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative dependency_composite values, meaning stronger composite dependency. KEAP1 and SMARCA4 remain extremely robust after stringent central-loss exclusion, high-quality screen restriction, and adenocarcinoma restriction. TP53 remains robust and independently validated. Iteration 6/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
The newly analyzed broad predictors are mostly below threshold or directionally unsupported. ERBB2 amplification does not support the claimed stronger-dependency direction either overall (signed +0.018, interval -0.094 to +0.131) or after excluding TP53/SMARCA4/KEAP1/PTEN losses (signed -0.009, interval -0.081 to +0.062). BRCA2 loss is also unsupported overall (signed -0.007) and in the central-loss-intact population (signed -0.061). NF1 loss is null for the claimed weaker-dependency direction overall (signed -0.002) and in the central-loss-intact population (signed -0.015). MTAP loss with CDKN2A intact in high-quality screens gives a small positive signed estimate of only +0.046, with an interval including zero and only marginally reaching the threshold; given earlier MTAP null results, this is not meaningful. Media serum 10% versus 5% is essentially null (signed +0.002), and Avana versus non-Avana library (signed -0.052) and matched RNA/DNA availability versus unmatched availability (signed +0.030) are also not threshold-level offsets. I therefore reject and close these hypotheses as not supporting scientifically meaningful associations in the claimed direction. These technical nulls are useful: they reduce concern that the central biological associations are simply platform, serum, or omics-availability artifacts, although residual confounding cannot be excluded.

The major new signal is MSI-high, but it is opposite the registered direction. H43 and H105 hypothesized that MSI-high is associated with higher composite scores, i.e. weaker dependency. Instead, the signed estimates are large and negative: -0.792 overall (interval -0.907 to -0.676) and -0.754 in the central-loss-intact population (interval -0.825 to -0.683). Because these are positive-direction claims, the negative signed estimates indicate that MSI-high cells have much lower, more negative dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency. The effect is far beyond the 0.15-unit threshold in the opposite direction and remains strong when TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN losses are excluded. I therefore reject H43 and H105 as written and close those investigations, but I register new reversed claims testing MSI-high as a predictor of stronger dependency: overall, central-loss-intact, and adenocarcinoma-restricted. I leave those proposals unresolved because the reversal is data-driven and should receive its own direct evidence signed to the reverse direction before any acceptance or validation decision.

Given the large observed reverse MSI-high signal, I do not request validation now. Validating the original positive-direction H43/H105 would test the same contrast under an inconvenient sign convention and would not by itself produce clean evidence for the reversed claim. The next analysis should first create direct reverse-direction evidence. I defer lower-priority untested subtype, library, and omics-availability flags, as well as untested MTAP main effects, because available evidence is strongly below threshold or technically null. The most useful next focus is to test the reversed MSI-high claims and, if direct signed evidence supports them, decide whether validation or context refinement is more informative.

both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
The newly delivered scheduled validation directly supports the positive TP53-loss claim. H13's independent validation gives a signed TP53-loss estimate of +0.356 with a conservative independent interval from +0.214 to +0.498. Both the point estimate and lower bound exceed the 0.15-unit threshold, so TP53 loss remains accepted as a strong within-dataset association with higher dependency_composite values, i.e. weaker composite dependency. H13 is therefore accepted and closed. The validation for H18 is a clean negative result: in the KEAP1-intact population, STK11 loss has a signed estimate of only +0.024, with an interval from -0.087 to +0.135. This is far below the threshold and the interval includes zero; it does not support a scientifically meaningful association of STK11 loss with stronger dependency. H18 is rejected and closed. These validations also reduce the concern that the main landscape is driven by technical or platform artifacts, because the major effects remain distinct even when STK11-loss and other contexts are tested separately.

The current supported within-dataset landscape is now broad and internally coherent. KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher, less negative dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency. SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative values, meaning stronger composite dependency. KEAP1 and SMARCA4 are extremely robust after stringent central-loss exclusion, high-quality-screen restriction, and adenocarcinoma restriction. TP53 is independently validated and robust across central-loss-excluded contexts. PTEN is accepted from its validated main effect and several robust contexts, although some narrower context estimates remain closer to the threshold. Negative or unsupported claimed associations include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, STK11 loss in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, RB1 loss in the claimed weaker-dependency direction, SMAD4 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, the constructed research markers, MTAP in central-loss-excluded contexts, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, media serum difference, CRISPR library offset, and matched omics-availability offset.

The major data-driven refinement is MSI-high. The originally registered positive-direction claims were rejected because the observed signed estimates were large and negative. The corresponding reverse claims now have the appropriately signed evidence. H120 gives a signed overall MSI-high effect of +0.792, interval +0.676 to +0.907, and H121 gives a signed effect of +0.754, interval +0.683 to +0.825, after excluding TP53, SMARCA4, KEAP1, and PTEN loss. Both are far beyond the threshold in the reverse direction. I therefore accept and keep active H120 and H121: MSI-high cells have substantially lower, more negative dependency_composite values, meaning stronger composite dependency, and this pattern is not explained by the four central losses. This is still a supplied-dataset association, not a causal effect, not a single-gene knockout measurement, and not a claim of external generalizability. The next priority is to understand where the MSI-high effect is robust and whether it is modified by lineage subtype, mutation burden, high-quality screens, or co-occurrence with TP53 loss. Proposed analyses focus on these contexts, with formal interactions to distinguish a broadly present association from genuine effect modification.

Iteration 7/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

record.narrative:
The strongest current conclusions are four central loss associations and a large reversed MSI-high association. KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher, less negative dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency, whereas SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative values, meaning stronger composite dependency. The new MSI-high signal is far above the 0.15-unit threshold in the stronger-dependency direction and is not removed by excluding the four central losses. The next priority is therefore not to rediscover these main effects but to ask where the MSI-high association is robust and whether it modifies the central landscape.

I register three MSI-high robustness proposals. First, central-loss-intact high-quality-screen MSI-high tests whether the reversed effect persists when both major co-driver losses and weaker-screen quality are removed. Second, central-loss-intact high mutation burden tests whether the association is still present among cells with elevated mutation burden, the context most likely to confound MSI-high status. Third, a formal interaction with the central-loss-intact subgroup tests whether the MSI-high association is materially different in cells lacking central losses versus cells with at least one central loss. These tests distinguish a broadly present MSI-high association from one limited to a small technical or mutational context.

I also register reciprocal stratification of the accepted central predictors by MSI status. Formal interactions ask whether the KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53 effects differ between MSI-high and MSI-negative cells. Because MSI-high cells may have distinct biology, these interactions ask whether the central dependency landscape is homogeneous or context-dependent. Direct within-MSI-high mean differences are registered for KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53 to estimate whether each central effect remains present in MSI-high cells, although these cells are small and the intervals may be wide. PTEN is too rare within MSI-high for a reliable positive-stratum test, so I register the larger MSI-negative context instead; this tests whether PTEN loss remains associated with stronger dependency when the small but strong MSI-high subgroup is excluded. All proposals remain supplied-dataset associations, not causal effects, single-gene knockout claims, or claims about external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 7/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

H122, H123, H126, and H127 test MSI-high robustness in the major adenocarcinoma subtype, high-quality screens, high mutation burden, and whether high mutation burden modifies the MSI-high association. H131 tests whether the MSI-high association differs when the four central losses are absent versus present. H132-H137 jointly assess the central landscape in MSI-high cells: interactions test whether KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53 effect sizes differ by MSI status, while direct within-MSI-high mean differences estimate whether each central association remains present among MSI-high cells. Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Continue validating only after direct context evidence is available.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The strongest current conclusions are four central loss associations and a large reversed MSI-high association. KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher, less negative dependency_composite values, meaning weaker composite dependency, whereas SMARCA4 loss and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative values, meaning stronger composite dependency. The new MSI-high signal is far above the 0.15-unit threshold in the stronger-dependency direction and is not removed by excluding the four central losses. The next priority is therefore not to rediscover these main effects but to ask where the MSI-high association is robust and whether it modifies the central landscape.\n\nI register three MSI-high robustness proposals. First, central-loss-intact high-quality-screen MSI-high tests whether the reversed effect persists when both major co-driver losses and weaker-screen quality are removed. Second, central-loss-intact high mutation burden tests whether the association is still present among cells with elevated mutation burden, the context most likely to confound MSI-high status. Third, a formal interaction with the central-loss-intact subgroup tests whether the MSI-high association is materially different in cells lacking central losses versus cells with at least one central loss. These tests distinguish a broadly present MSI-high association from one limited to a small technical or mutational context.\n\nI also register reciprocal stratification of the accepted central predictors by MSI status.
