Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Iteration 10/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

These new proposals extend the accepted within-dataset landscape through broader context and technical-boundary tests rather than re-testing well-established main effects. First, I register KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and TP53 loss in MSI-negative cells with high whole-genome ploidy (upper-quartile ploidy >=3.048). The expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrasts are positive for KEAP1 and TP53, meaning higher or less negative dependency_composite and weaker dependency, and negative for SMARCA4, meaning lower or more negative dependency_composite and stronger dependency. Plausible alternatives include attenuation or absence of the accepted effects if the associations are driven mainly by non-high-ploidy contexts or if ploidy itself dominates the composite score. Next, I test whether the same three predictors remain associated with the accepted directions inside MSI-negative, lower-quality screen cells defined by screen_roc_auc <=0.9298, the lower quartile. This is a technical robustness test: persistence of intervals above the 0.15-unit threshold would support descriptive stability even when screen separation is weaker; attenuation or null results would limit generalization even within this supplied dataset and could indicate that accepted effects are more visible in high-quality screens. I then add high hypoxia contexts for SMARCA4 and PTEN in MSI-negative cells. KEAP1 in high hypoxia is already accepted; SMARCA4 is a key accepted stronger-dependency predictor, and PTEN is a moderate accepted predictor that may be sensitive to stress contexts. Expected raw signs follow the accepted main effects, with possible attenuation if hypoxia reflects general screen state rather than context-specific biology. For MSI-high, I test high growth rate (doublings/day >=0.6), asking whether the very strong stronger-dependency association persists in fast-proliferating cells; attenuation would suggest the MSI-high contrast depends on slower-growing cells. For PTEN, I test both high growth and a median-split EMT context in MSI-negative cells. The median-split EMT proposal refines the earlier upper-quartile EMT test H156, which had a subthreshold lower bound and small exposed cell count (R114); using the EMT median threshold (>=0.043) improves power while preserving a plausible stress/differentiation boundary, though the context is less extreme. Finally, I register a main-effect screen_batch_a versus batch_b comparison to quantify technical batch variation in the composite score. This is not a biological hypothesis; it is a confounding and descriptive-generalizability check. If batch differences exceed 0.15 units, some associations could be more context-dependent. All comparisons remain supplied-dataset associations under explicit eligibility and subgroup definitions, not causal effects, single-gene knockout effects, or claims of external generalizability.","analyze":"No assessments are due. H168-H170 test whether KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and TP53 loss remain associated with the accepted directions in MSI-negative lower-quality screen cells (screen_roc_auc <= 0.9298). H165-H167 test KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53 in MSI-negative high-ploidy cells (ploidy >= 3.048), a boundary broader than the accepted high-aneuploidy tests. H175 tests PTEN loss in MSI-negative median-or-high EMT cells, refining the underpowered upper-quartile EMT check. H171-H174 test SMARCA4 and PTEN in MSI-negative high-hypoxia cells and MSI-high or PTEN in high-growth-rate cells. H176 quantifies batch_a versus batch_b variation in the composite dependency score as a technical confounding check. Estimates and intervals are interpreted as already signed to each claim direction: positive signed estimates for KEAP1/TP53 positive-direction claims correspond to higher, less negative scores, i.e. weaker dependency; positive signed estimates for SMARCA4, MSI-high, and PTEN negative-direction claims correspond to lower, more negative scores, i.e. stronger dependency. All requested analyses are within-dataset association contrasts, not causal or externally generalizable effects. In high stemness MSI-negative contexts, KEAP1 H153 and SMARCA4 H154 are robust. In high EMT MSI-negative contexts, SMARCA4 H155 remains very strong, while PTEN H156 has a point estimate above threshold but its interval lower bound is only +0.081, so threshold-level evidence in the claimed direction is not established and the comparison is kept unresolved. I defer H156 because the exposed cell is small, n=56, and PTEN has broader accepted associations already; spending more investigation on this single underpowered context is lower priority than confirming the more informative PTEN context. H114, H116, H118, and H157 show that TP53 loss in high mutation burden, KEAP1 loss in high hypoxia, SMARCA4 loss in high growth rate, and MSI-high in median-high SLFN11 contexts all have intervals whose lower bounds exceed the threshold in the claimed direction, so I accept and close them. The important borderline claim is H149: PTEN loss in MSI-negative cells with KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53 intact gives signed +0.260 with lower +0.182 and n=122/839. This is acceptable under the discovery 95% criterion, but it is close enough and context-specific enough to warrant independent validation; I therefore accept it for now, keep H149 active, and request validation. record.narrative: The twelve new contrasts largely reinforce the accepted supplied-dataset predictor landscape. For positive-direction KEAP1 and TP53 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed cell has a higher, less negative dependency_composite score, i.e. weaker composite dependency. For negative-direction SMARCA4, MSI-high, and PTEN claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed cell has a lower, more negative score, i.e. stronger composite dependency. H165 and H166 show that KEAP1 loss and SMARCA4 loss remain robust in MSI-negative high-ploidy contexts, with signed estimates around +0.92 and +0.93 and lower bounds far above the 0.15-unit threshold. H167, TP53 loss in MSI-negative high-ploidy contexts, is positive and above threshold at +0.400, with lower bound +0.188; I accept it as threshold-supported but note it is relatively borderline and should not be overinterpreted beyond this dataset. In lower-quality screen cells, defined by MSI-negative status and screen_roc_auc <= 0.9298, KEAP1 loss H168 and SMARCA4 loss H169 remain strong, with lower bounds above +0.68. TP53 loss H170 is directionally positive and large (+0.352), but its 95% lower bound is only +0.133, below the meaningful-effect threshold. I therefore keep H170 unresolved and request independent validation; if validation clears threshold, this would support context-specific robustness despite weaker screen separation, whereas failure would limit generalization to lower-quality screens within this dataset without undermining the accepted main TP53 association. High-hypoxia and high-growth contexts support accepted SMARCA4 effects (H171, H173) and a moderate PTEN effect in high-growth MSI-negative cells (H174, lower bound +0.192), though H174 is also small in exposed cells and should be treated as moderate. PTEN contexts H172 and H175 are directionally positive but do not establish threshold-level evidence because lower bounds are below 0.15; they remain unresolved/deferred rather than accepted. H176 tests batch_a versus batch_b as a technical confounding check. The signed estimate is effectively null (-0.011) with an interval well within the threshold range, so I reject the claim of a meaningful batch_a-versus-batch_b main difference. This reduces concern about a simple batch_a/batch_b offset but does not exclude other batch contrasts or context-dependent batch effects. Overall, multiplicity and conditioning remain important: these are many non-adjusted eligibility and subgroup contrasts, and subgroup selection could induce selection bias. The conclusions remain within-dataset associations under explicit contrasts, not causal effects or externally generalizable biological claims.

Iteration 10/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

These new proposals extend the accepted within-dataset landscape through broader context and technical-boundary tests rather than re-testing well-established main effects. First, I register KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and TP53 loss in MSI-negative cells with high whole-genome ploidy (upper-quartile ploidy >=3.048). The expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrasts are positive for KEAP1 and TP53, meaning higher or less negative dependency_composite and weaker dependency, and negative for SMARCA4, meaning lower or more negative dependency_composite and stronger dependency. Plausible alternatives include attenuation or absence of the accepted effects if the associations are driven mainly by non-high-ploidy contexts or if ploidy itself dominates the composite score. Next, I test whether the same three predictors remain associated with the accepted directions inside MSI-negative, lower-quality screen cells defined by screen_roc_auc <=0.9298, the lower quartile. This is a technical robustness test: persistence of intervals above the 0.15-unit threshold would support descriptive stability even when screen separation is weaker; attenuation or null results would limit generalization even within this supplied dataset and could indicate that accepted effects are more visible in high-quality screens. I then add high hypoxia contexts for SMARCA4 and PTEN in MSI-negative cells. KEAP1 in high hypoxia is already accepted; SMARCA4 is a key accepted stronger-dependency predictor, and PTEN is a moderate accepted predictor that may be sensitive to stress contexts. Expected raw signs follow the accepted main effects, with possible attenuation if hypoxia reflects general screen state rather than context-specific biology. For MSI-high, I test high growth rate (doublings/day >=0.6), asking whether the very strong stronger-dependency association persists in fast-proliferating cells; attenuation would suggest the MSI-high contrast depends on slower-growing cells. For PTEN, I test both high growth and a median-split EMT context in MSI-negative cells. The median-split EMT proposal refines the earlier upper-quartile EMT test H156, which had a subthreshold lower bound and small exposed cell count (R114); using the EMT median threshold (>=0.043) improves power while preserving a plausible stress/differentiation boundary, though the context is less extreme. Finally, I register a main-effect screen_batch_a versus batch_b comparison to quantify technical batch variation in the composite score. This is not a biological hypothesis; it is a confounding and descriptive-generalizability check. If batch differences exceed 0.15 units, some associations could be more context-dependent. All comparisons remain supplied-dataset associations under explicit eligibility and subgroup definitions, not causal effects, single-gene knockout effects, or claims of external generalizability.","analyze":"No assessments are due. I selected twelve active, previously untested comparisons that probe robustness and boundary conditions for the central accepted predictors, prioritizing lower-quality screen contexts and high-ploidy contexts, followed by PTEN median-EMT, hypoxia/growth contexts, and a batch main-effect check. H168-H170 test whether KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and TP53 loss remain associated with the accepted directions in MSI-negative lower-quality screen cells (screen_roc_auc <= 0.9298). H165-H167 test KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53 in MSI-negative high-ploidy cells (ploidy >= 3.048), a boundary broader than the accepted high-aneuploidy tests. H175 tests PTEN loss in MSI-negative median-or-high EMT cells, refining the underpowered upper-quartile EMT check. H171-H174 test SMARCA4 and PTEN in MSI-negative high-hypoxia cells and MSI-high or PTEN in high-growth-rate cells. H176 quantifies batch_a versus batch_b variation in the composite dependency score as a technical confounding check. Estimates and intervals are interpreted as already signed to each claim direction: positive signed estimates for KEAP1/TP53 positive-direction claims correspond to higher, less negative scores, i.e. weaker dependency; positive signed estimates for SMARCA4, MSI-high, and PTEN negative-direction claims correspond to lower, more negative scores, i.e. stronger dependency. All requested analyses are within-dataset association contrasts, not causal or externally generalizable effects. I also closed H121 because its accepted MSI-high effect in the four-loss-absent MSI-negative population is strong on discovery evidence and does not require validation to accept as a within-dataset claim.","appraise":"The twelve new contrasts largely reinforce the accepted supplied-dataset predictor landscape. For negative-direction SMARCA4, MSI-high, and PTEN claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed cell has a lower, more negative score, i.e. stronger composite dependency. H165 and H166 show that KEAP1 loss and SMARCA4 loss remain robust in MSI-negative high-ploidy contexts, with signed estimates around +0.92 and +0.93 and lower bounds far above the 0.15-unit threshold. H167, TP53 loss in MSI-negative high-ploidy contexts, is positive and above threshold at +0.400, with lower bound +0.188; I accept it as threshold-supported but note it is relatively borderline and should not be overinterpreted beyond this dataset. In lower-quality screen cells, defined by MSI-negative status and screen_roc_auc <= 0.9298, KEAP1 loss H168 and SMARCA4 loss H169 remain strong, with lower bounds above +0.68. TP53 loss H170 is directionally positive and large (+0.352), but its 95% lower bound is only +0.133, below the meaningful-effect threshold. I therefore keep H170 unresolved and request independent validation; if validation clears threshold, this would support context-specific robustness despite weaker screen separation, whereas failure would limit generalization to lower-quality screens within this dataset without undermining the accepted main TP53 association. High-hypoxia and high-growth contexts support accepted SMARCA4 effects (H171, H173) and a moderate PTEN effect in high-growth MSI-negative cells (H174, lower bound +0.192), though H174 is also small in exposed cells and should be treated as moderate. PTEN contexts H172 and H175 are directionally positive but do not establish threshold-level evidence because lower bounds are below 0.15; they remain unresolved/deferred rather than accepted. H176 tests batch_a versus batch_b as a technical confounding check. The signed estimate is effectively null (-0.011) with an interval well within the threshold range, so I reject the claim of a meaningful batch_a-versus-batch_b main difference. This reduces concern about a simple batch_a/batch_b offset but does not exclude other batch contrasts or context-dependent batch effects. Overall, multiplicity and conditioning remain important: these are many non-adjusted eligibility and subgroup contrasts, and subgroup selection could induce selection bias. The new H149 validation is also consistent but more borderline. record.narrative: The new validation resolves the boundary uncertainty for TP53 loss in lower-quality screens and confirms the core TP53 association. H170, TP53 loss in MSI-negative cells with lower screen separation, had a discovery signed estimate of +0.352 with lower bound +0.133, below the 0.15-unit meaningful-effect threshold. The independent validation signed estimate is +0.583 with lower bound +0.322, well above threshold and excluding both null and threshold-level uncertainty. I accept H170 and close it. This means that, within this supplied dataset, TP53 loss is associated with a higher, less negative dependency_composite value, i.e. weaker composite dependency, even in the lower screen-quality stratum. H145 remains a narrow, high-quality screen, all-loss-absent MSI-negative context for PTEN loss. Its discovery signed estimate was +0.255 with a 95% lower bound of +0.157, but the independent validation signed estimate was +0.255 with lower bound +0.094, which does not clear the 0.15-unit threshold under the stringent independent interval. I keep H145 unresolved and close the investigation: the point estimates are directionally supportive, but the validation interval leaves uncertainty about whether this very narrow stratum exceeds the meaningful-effect threshold. This does not undermine broader accepted PTEN associations, including H37, H49, H70, H149, and related context tests. H81, the KEAP1-loss association modified by PTEN-positive status in the claimed positive direction, was not supported. Discovery gave a small positive signed estimate of +0.145 and validation gave +0.093, with validation interval crossing null. I reject H81 and close it. This argues against a meaningful positive interaction between KEAP1 and PTEN for the claimed direction; it does not establish exact absence of all interaction, but the available evidence does not support a threshold-level KEAP1-by-PTEN modification. Overall, the accepted within-dataset landscape remains robust: KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are associated with higher, less negative dependency_composite scores, i.e. weaker dependency, whereas SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high status, and PTEN loss are associated with lower, more negative scores, i.e. stronger dependency. KEAP1, SMARCA4, TP53, and MSI-high effects are large and validated in several contexts; PTEN effects are moderate and generally around +0.22 to +0.27 signed units, with some near-threshold contexts remaining unresolved. Rejected negative findings include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, many MTAP contexts, research markers D/E/F, media serum contrast, matched omics availability, Avana library as a main effect, and batch_a versus batch_b main effect. Interaction claims are mostly unsupported or unresolved. The most informative next work should avoid additional tiny co-loss strata and instead focus on broad near-threshold main-effect contexts and technical coherence, such as PTEN in KEAP1-intact or SMARCA4-intact contexts, MSI-high with IFN-related or SLFN11-related contexts, and broad batch/library robustness tests if they have sufficient cell counts. All conclusions remain supplied-dataset associations under explicit contrasts, not causal effects, single-gene knockout claims, or externally generalizable biological claims.

These new proposals extend the accepted within-dataset landscape through broader context and technical-boundary tests rather than re-testing well-established main effects. First, I register KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and TP53 loss in MSI-negative cells with high whole-genome ploidy (upper-quartile ploidy >=3.048). The expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrasts are positive for KEAP1 and TP53, meaning higher or less negative dependency_composite and weaker dependency, and negative for SMARCA4, meaning lower or more negative dependency_composite and stronger dependency. Plausible alternatives include attenuation or absence of the accepted effects if the associations are driven mainly by non-high-ploidy contexts or if ploidy itself dominates the composite score. Next, I test whether the same three predictors remain associated with the accepted directions inside MSI-negative, lower-quality screen cells defined by screen_roc_auc <=0.9298, the lower quartile. This is a technical robustness test: persistence of intervals above the 0.15-unit threshold would support descriptive stability even when screen separation is weaker; attenuation or null results would limit generalization even within this supplied dataset and could indicate that accepted effects are more visible in high-quality screens. I then add high hypoxia contexts for SMARCA4 and PTEN in MSI-negative cells. KEAP1 in high hypoxia is already accepted; SMARCA4 is a key accepted stronger-dependency predictor, and PTEN is a moderate accepted predictor that may be sensitive to stress contexts. Expected raw signs follow the accepted main effects, with possible attenuation if hypoxia reflects general screen state rather than context-specific biology. For MSI-high, I test high growth rate (doublings/day >=0.6), asking whether the very strong stronger-dependency association persists in fast-proliferating cells; attenuation would suggest the MSI-high contrast depends on slower-growing cells. For PTEN, I test both high growth and a median-split EMT context in MSI-negative cells. The median-split EMT proposal refines the earlier upper-quartile EMT test H156, which had a subthreshold lower bound and small exposed cell count (R114); using the EMT median threshold (>=0.043) improves power while preserving a plausible stress/differentiation boundary, though the context is less extreme. Finally, I register a main-effect screen_batch_a versus batch_b comparison to quantify technical batch variation in the composite score. This is not a biological hypothesis; it is a confounding and descriptive-generalizability check. If batch differences exceed 0.15 units, some associations could be more context-dependent. H165-H167 test KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53 in MSI-negative high-ploidy cells (ploidy >= 3.048), a boundary broader than the accepted high-aneuploidy tests. H175 tests PTEN loss in MSI-negative median-or-high EMT cells, refining the underpowered upper-quartile EMT check. H171-H174 test SMARCA4 and PTEN in MSI-negative high-hypoxia cells and MSI-high or PTEN in high-growth-rate cells. H176 quantifies batch_a versus batch_b variation in the composite dependency score as a technical confounding check. Iteration 11/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

Iteration 11/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The twelve new discovery contrasts strengthen the central supplied-dataset predictor landscape while clarifying several technical and near-threshold caveats. I use the ledger's signed-direction convention: for positive-direction KEAP1 and TP53 claims, a positive signed estimate means higher/less negative dependency_composite, i.e. weaker composite dependency; for negative-direction SMARCA4, MSI-high, PTEN, and CDKN2A claims, a positive signed estimate means lower/more negative scores, i.e. stronger composite dependency. H178, H179, and H180 test whether KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and TP53-loss contrasts persist among cells with high measured Cas9 activity (cas9_activity_pct >= 88.9). All three remain above the 0.15-unit threshold, with H178 signed +0.735 (lower +0.594), H179 signed +0.691 (lower +0.536), and H180 signed +0.396 (lower +0.198). I accept all three, although H180 is more borderline and Cas9-activity data are not complete, so this is descriptive robustness in a measured high-Cas9 subset rather than a causal or generalizable perturbation-quality claim. H47 and H48 show that TP53-loss association also persists in adenocarcinoma and higher screen-quality contexts, with signed estimates +0.414 and +0.462 and lower bounds well above threshold; both are accepted and closed. H158 shows that the MSI-high stronger-dependency association persists in the median-or-high IFN-gamma signature stratum, signed +0.811 (lower +0.677), and is accepted. H177 is the most informative PTEN result: in a broad TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative context, the signed PTEN-loss estimate is +0.255 with lower bound +0.168, just clearing the threshold. I provisionally accept it because the 95% discovery interval clears the practical threshold, but I keep H177 active and request independent validation because it is near the threshold and could materially affect confidence in a broad PTEN context without disturbing the broader accepted PTEN landscape. H182, H183, and H112 are directionally supportive PTEN contrasts with point estimates above threshold, but their lower bounds are far below 0.15 (H182 +0.066, H183 +0.047, H112 +0.065), so they remain unresolved and deferred; independent validation is unlikely to resolve them under stringent independent intervals compared with H177. H181 is a broad CDKN2A test in MSI-negative, TP53-intact cells. Its signed estimate is +0.146, below the threshold, with lower bound +0.073 and upper bound +0.220. This is a perturbation-quality boundary test: if the accepted main associations persist there, it supports descriptive robustness across a technical stratum with stronger measured Cas9 signal; attenuation or nullity would limit within-dataset generalization to high-Cas9 cells without refuting the broader main effects. Claims 7-9 ask whether KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and TP53-loss contrasts differ between adherent-culture cells and their complement. The anticipated interaction is uncertain; a threshold-level interaction would indicate context dependence, whereas a small interaction interval would support relative stability across the predominant culture condition. Claims 10-12 are median-split research-signature interactions for KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53, respectively. Because these constructed signatures have no assigned biological role, the scientific question is narrower: do standardized assay strata mark effect modification of the established within-dataset associations? All three remain above the 0.15-unit threshold, with H178 signed +0.735 (lower +0.594), H179 signed +0.691 (lower +0.536), and H180 signed +0.396 (lower +0.198). H158 shows that the MSI-high stronger-dependency association persists in the median-or-high IFN-gamma signature stratum, signed +0.811 (lower +0.677), and is accepted. H177 is the most informative PTEN result: in a broad TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative context, the signed PTEN-loss estimate is +0.255 with lower bound +0.168, just clearing the threshold. I provisionally accept it because the 95% discovery interval clears the practical threshold, but I keep H177 active and request independent validation because it is near the threshold and could materially affect confidence in a broad PTEN context without disturbing the broader accepted PTEN landscape. H182, H183, and H112 are directionally supportive PTEN contrasts with point estimates above threshold, but their lower bounds are far below 0.15 (H182 +0.066, H183 +0.047, H112 +0.065), so they remain unresolved and deferred; independent validation is unlikely to resolve them under stringent independent intervals compared with H177. Because the interval still crosses the threshold, I do not reject exact absence, but I leave it unresolved and defer further CDKN2A work: across several adequately powered contexts, CDKN2A has not produced a convincing threshold-supported effect. Due validation assessments:
H149: PTEN-loss compared with PTEN-intact among cells that are KEAP1-loss absent, SMARCA4-loss absent, TP53-loss absent, and MSI-negative. The signed estimates use the negative-direction claim convention, so positive signed values correspond to raw exposed-minus-comparator scores being more negative, i.e. stronger composite dependency. Discovery gave signed +0.260 (95% lower bound +0.182), and independent validation gave signed +0.271 with a stringent lower bound +0.151. The validation lower bound just clears the 0.15-unit practical threshold and the point estimates are stable across discovery and validation. I therefore accept H149 and close it as a validated supplied-dataset association.
H177: PTEN-loss compared with PTEN-intact in a broader TP53-intact/SMARCA4-intact/MSI-negative context. Discovery signed estimate was +0.255 with lower bound +0.168, so the 95% discovery interval cleared the threshold. The independent validation signed estimate was +0.233, but the stringent interval had lower bound +0.095, so it does not exclude threshold-level uncertainty. The direction remains supportive, but under the independent interval this specific broad context is not confirmed above the meaningful-effect threshold. I therefore downgrade H177 to unresolved and close this specific context investigation. This does not refute the broader PTEN landscape accepted from H149 and other contexts, but it marks H177 as an unresolved boundary case.

Overall final scientific report:
The strongest and most robust within-dataset associations are large effects in a composite dependency score. For positive-direction claims about KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss, positive signed estimates mean the exposed group has higher, less negative dependency_composite values, i.e. weaker composite dependency. For negative-direction claims about SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high status, and PTEN loss, positive signed estimates mean the exposed group has lower, more negative dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency.

Supported findings in this supplied dataset: KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker composite dependency across many contexts, with signed contrasts generally around +0.73 to +0.93 and validated overall and in several strata. TP53 loss is also associated with weaker composite dependency, with signed contrasts generally around +0.36 to +0.58 and validated in several contexts, including lower-quality and high-Cas9 strata. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger composite dependency, with signed contrasts generally around +0.62 to +0.93 and validated overall and in several strata. MSI-high status is associated with stronger composite dependency, with signed contrasts generally around +0.74 to +0.86 and validated overall and in multiple biologically distinct strata, including adenocarcinoma, higher screen-quality, IFN-related, SLFN11-related, and growth-rate-related subsets. PTEN loss is associated with moderate stronger composite dependency. The validated H149 contrast is approximately +0.27 signed units, just clearing threshold in the stringent validation interval, and several other PTEN contexts are accepted or near-threshold. However, PTEN is more context-sensitive and less precisely bounded than the big effects: H177 was downgraded to unresolved after validation failed to exclude threshold-level uncertainty, and several PTEN strata remain unresolved or deferred.

Negative or insufficient findings: There is no threshold-level evidence that KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, research marker D, research marker E, research marker F, media serum contrast, matched omics availability, Avana library as a main effect, or batch_a versus batch_b as a main effect is meaningfully associated with the composite dependency score under the tested contrasts. CDKN2A is not convincingly supported: its broad MSI-negative/TP53-intact contrast has point estimate near but below threshold, and earlier accepted CDKN2A contrasts have been moved to unresolved or otherwise remain weak. Interaction claims are mostly unsupported, rejected, or unresolved; no robust epistasis or modifier effect is established. Rejected interaction examples include the claimed KEAP1-by-PTEN positive modification and the claimed SMARCA4-by-KEAP1 negative modification, while several interactions remain only exploratory or low-powered.

Technical robustness and boundary interpretation: The KEAP1, SMARCA4, and TP53 main effects persist in high measured Cas9-activity cells, which supports descriptive robustness within a stronger perturbation-quality subset. TP53 loss also remains supported in adenocarcinoma, higher screen-quality, high mutation-burden, high ploidy, and low screen-quality strata. MSI-high remains strongly supported across several marker-defined strata. These are still association patterns in the supplied dataset, not causal perturbation effects, not single-gene knockout claims, and not externally generalizable biological claims. The endpoint is composite, and research signatures/markers have arbitrary or no assigned biological meaning.

Most informative next work: The next analyses should focus on the remaining moderate but important PTEN-loss landscape rather than adding more tiny co-loss strata. I registered direct PTEN-loss contrasts in high measured Cas9-activity cells and inside KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and TP53-loss contexts to ask whether the moderate PTEN association remains additive within dominant technical and predictor strata. Existing unresolved PTEN-by-KEAP1 and PTEN-by-SMARCA4 interaction comparisons may also be useful, but they should be interpreted only as exploratory effect modification unless interval evidence excludes threshold-level uncertainty. record.narrative: No assessments are due. I register ten new supplied-dataset comparisons that deepen follow-up on the moderate PTEN-loss landscape and add robustness checks for the two dominant large predictor contrasts. For negative-direction PTEN-loss claims, positive signed estimates correspond to raw exposed-minus-comparator scores that are more negative, i.e. stronger composite dependency. For positive-direction KEAP1-loss claims, positive signed estimates correspond to higher, less negative scores, i.e. weaker composite dependency. For SMARCA4-loss, negative direction is again interpreted as stronger composite dependency. Claims 1-8 focus on PTEN. Claim 1 tests whether the PTEN-loss contrast differs between adenocarcinoma cells and the non-adenocarcinoma complement, addressing lineage dependence of the moderate PTEN association. Claims 2 and 3 test PTEN-loss in high screen-quality (screen_roc_auc >= 0.95) and low screen-quality (<=0.9298) cells; high-quality testing is important because PTEN was validated in a clean high-quality context, while low-quality testing probes whether the moderate association survives poorer screen discrimination. Claims 4 and 5 test effect modification by measured Cas9 activity and the direct low-Cas9 boundary contrast, extending H190 high-Cas9 testing and asking whether the PTEN association is robust when measured Cas9 signal is lower. Claim 6 tests PTEN-by-TP53-loss interaction, which is distinct from the already registered mean PTEN effect within TP53-loss cells and asks whether TP53-loss context changes the size of the PTEN contrast. Claims 7 and 8 test PTEN interaction with median-or-high ploidy and adherent culture, giving genomic-instability and technical-culture boundary checks. Claims 9 and 10 test KEAP1 loss and SMARCA4 loss among high mutation-burden cells, complementing existing high-TMB tests for TP53 and PTEN and asking whether the very large KEAP1 and SMARCA4 landscape patterns persist in a high-TMB subset. These are all descriptive association contrasts under explicit definitions, not causal effects, single-gene knockout claims, or externally generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 12/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

For positive-direction KEAP1-loss claims, positive signed estimates correspond to higher, less negative scores, i.e. weaker composite dependency. For SMARCA4-loss, negative direction is again interpreted as stronger composite dependency. Claims 1-8 focus on PTEN. Claim 1 tests whether the PTEN-loss contrast differs between adenocarcinoma cells and the non-adenocarcinoma complement, addressing lineage dependence of the moderate PTEN association. Claims 2 and 3 test PTEN-loss in high screen-quality (screen_roc_auc >= 0.95) and low screen-quality (<=0.9298) cells; high-quality testing is important because PTEN was validated in a clean high-quality context, while low-quality testing probes whether the moderate association survives poorer screen discrimination. Claim 6 tests PTEN-by-TP53-loss interaction, which is distinct from the already registered mean PTEN effect within TP53-loss cells and asks whether TP53-loss context changes the size of the PTEN contrast. Claims 7 and 8 test PTEN interaction with median-or-high ploidy and adherent culture, giving genomic-instability and technical-culture boundary checks. Claims 9 and 10 test KEAP1 loss and SMARCA4 loss among high mutation-burden cells, complementing existing high-TMB tests for TP53 and PTEN and asking whether the very large KEAP1 and SMARCA4 landscape patterns persist in a high-TMB subset. record.narrative: No assessments are due, and no independent validation request is available because the remaining new validation allowance is zero. I therefore request twelve new supplied-dataset discovery contrasts from previously registered active claims that have no evidence in the ledger. These tests are intended to allocate analysis efficiently by probing (1) whether the very large KEAP1-loss and SMARCA4-loss associations persist in a high mutation-burden subset and (2) whether the moderate PTEN-loss association remains threshold-supported across biologically and technically meaningful boundary contexts. The selected comparisons are Welch two-sample contrasts on dependency_composite, with 95% intervals and the controller's minimum-cell-size safeguard of 20 observations per comparison cell. The returned estimates will already be signed to the claim direction: for positive-direction KEAP1-loss claims, positive signed values indicate higher, less negative dependency_composite values, i.e. weaker composite dependency; for negative-direction SMARCA4-loss and PTEN-loss claims, positive signed values indicate lower, more negative dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency. H190 and H198 test PTEN-loss in high and low measured Cas9-activity strata, giving technical-quality boundary checks. H191, H192, and H193 test PTEN-loss inside KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and TP53-loss contexts, respectively, asking whether the moderate PTEN signal persists in the major predictor strata. H194 tests whether PTEN-loss differs between adenocarcinoma and the complementary lineage-subtype group. H195 tests PTEN-loss among higher screen-quality cells. If PTEN main contrasts remain around or above 0.15 signed units with intervals clearing the threshold, PTEN can be regarded as a robust moderate predictor in the supplied dataset.
