Iteration 12/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

I use the ledger's signed-direction convention: for positive-direction KEAP1 and TP53 claims, a positive signed estimate means higher/less negative dependency_composite, i.e. weaker composite dependency; for negative-direction SMARCA4, MSI-high, PTEN, and CDKN2A claims, a positive signed estimate means lower/more negative scores, i.e. stronger composite dependency. H178, H179, and H180 test whether KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and TP53-loss contrasts persist among cells with high measured Cas9 activity (cas9_activity_pct >= 88.9). All three remain above the 0.15-unit threshold, with H178 signed +0.735 (lower +0.594), H179 signed +0.691 (lower +0.536), and H180 signed +0.396 (lower +0.198). I accept all three, although H180 is more borderline and Cas9-activity data are not complete, so this is descriptive robustness in a measured high-Cas9 subset rather than a causal or generalizable perturbation-quality claim. H47 and H48 show that TP53-loss association also persists in adenocarcinoma and higher screen-quality contexts, with signed estimates +0.414 and +0.462 and lower bounds well above threshold; both are accepted and closed. H158 shows that the MSI-high stronger-dependency association persists in the median-or-high IFN-gamma signature stratum, signed +0.811 (lower +0.677), and is accepted. H177 is the most informative PTEN result: in a broad TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative context, the signed PTEN-loss estimate is +0.255 with lower bound +0.168, just clearing the threshold. I provisionally accept it because the 95% discovery interval clears the practical threshold, but I keep H177 active and request independent validation because it is near the threshold and could materially affect confidence in a broad PTEN context without disturbing the broader accepted PTEN landscape. H182, H183, and H112 are directionally supportive PTEN contrasts with point estimates above threshold, but their lower bounds are far below 0.15 (H182 +0.066, H183 +0.047, H112 +0.065), so they remain unresolved and deferred; independent validation is unlikely to resolve them under stringent independent intervals compared with H177. H181 is a broad CDKN2A test in MSI-negative, TP53-intact cells. Its signed estimate is +0.146, below the threshold, with lower bound +0.073 and upper bound +0.220. Because the interval still crosses the threshold, I do not reject exact absence, but I leave it unresolved and defer further CDKN2A work: across several adequately powered contexts, CDKN2A has not produced a convincing threshold-supported effect. This prompted reassessment of prior borderline accepted CDKN2A and PTEN claims: H88 remains unresolved and closed because its validation point estimate is below threshold and its independent interval is broad, and H138 is moved from accepted to unresolved because its lower bound (+0.138) does not clear the threshold despite a supportive point estimate. H20, the SMARCA4-by-KEAP1 interaction, is rejected for the claimed negative interaction: the signed interval [-0.167, +0.121] excludes a meaningful negative interaction in the hypothesized direction and centers near null. Overall, multiplicity and selection over subgroups remain relevant. These are unadjusted descriptive contrasts, not causal effects, single-gene knockout mechanisms, or external generalizations. PTEN loss is associated with moderate stronger composite dependency. The validated H149 contrast is approximately +0.27 signed units, just clearing threshold in the stringent validation interval, and several other PTEN contexts are accepted or near-threshold. However, PTEN is more context-sensitive and less precisely bounded than the big effects: H177 was downgraded to unresolved after validation failed to exclude threshold-level uncertainty, and several PTEN strata remain unresolved or deferred.\n\nNegative or insufficient findings: There is no threshold-level evidence that KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, research marker D, research marker E, research marker F, media serum contrast, matched omics availability, Avana library as a main effect, or batch_a versus batch_b as a main effect is meaningfully associated with the composite dependency score under the tested contrasts. CDKN2A is not convincingly supported: its broad MSI-negative/TP53-intact contrast has point estimate near but below threshold, and earlier accepted CDKN2A contrasts have been moved to unresolved or otherwise remain weak. Interaction claims are mostly unsupported, rejected, or unresolved; no robust epistasis or modifier effect is established. These are still association patterns in the supplied dataset, not causal perturbation effects, not single-gene knockout claims, and not externally generalizable biological claims. I registered direct PTEN-loss contrasts in high measured Cas9-activity cells and inside KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and TP53-loss contexts to ask whether the moderate PTEN association remains additive within dominant technical and predictor strata. record.narrative: The new evidence largely reinforces the dominant within-dataset landscape while making the PTEN-loss picture more nuanced. Using the signed-direction convention: for positive-direction KEAP1-loss claims, positive signed estimates mean higher/less negative dependency_composite, i.e. weaker composite dependency; for negative-direction SMARCA4-loss and PTEN-loss claims, positive signed estimates mean lower/more negative scores, i.e. stronger composite dependency. H202 shows that the large KEAP1-loss weaker-dependency association persists in high mutation-burden cells, signed +0.831 with 95% lower bound +0.695; H203 similarly shows the large SMARCA4-loss stronger-dependency association persists in high mutation-burden cells, signed +0.846 with lower bound +0.701. Both clear the 0.15-unit threshold decisively and are accepted and closed. H191 is important for PTEN: within KEAP1-loss cells, PTEN-loss remains associated with stronger composite dependency, signed +0.378 with lower bound +0.193, so PTEN evidence is not merely an artifact of excluding KEAP1-loss and is accepted and closed. By contrast, H192 and H193, the direct PTEN contrasts within SMARCA4-loss and TP53-loss cells, remain unresolved: H192 signed +0.132 lower -0.060, and H193 signed +0.102 lower -0.187. These may reflect weaker effects in these strata or reduced power, but neither provides threshold-cleared independent support for that specific conditional main effect. They are deferred rather than accepted. H69, PTEN-loss in a broad KEAP1-intact and SMARCA4-intact context, is directionally supportive but borderline, signed +0.240 with lower bound +0.141. Because the lower bound does not clear the practical threshold and no validation capacity remains, I leave it unresolved and deferred. This does not overturn the broader PTEN evidence from prior accepted/validated PTEN contrasts; it marks this specific subgroup as not independently threshold-cleared. H163 tests PTEN in high mutation-burden cells and is underpowered, signed +0.162 with interval crossing zero and threshold; unresolved and deferred. H164 tests the PTEN-by-high-TMB interaction and is rejected because the claimed positive signed interaction upper bound is +0.136, below the 0.15 threshold, with an estimate centered near zero. H194, PTEN-by-adenocarcinoma interaction, is not supported: signed -0.069 with a broad interval. The upper bound is only marginally above threshold, so I classify it unresolved and deferred rather than claiming formal rejection. H195, PTEN among higher screen-quality cells, is near-threshold but imprecise, signed +0.161 lower +0.037; unresolved and deferred. The Cas9-activity boundary tests are especially informative for PTEN: high Cas9 H190 is supportive but imprecise, signed +0.209 lower +0.010, while low Cas9 H198 is larger but still not threshold-cleared, signed +0.339 lower +0.131. Because PTEN within TP53-loss H193 is attenuated, I register refinements testing PTEN-loss in Cas9-high and Cas9-low contexts restricted to TP53-intact cells. These could help determine whether the moderate PTEN association persists cleanly when a likely attenuation source is removed. H190 and H198 remain active for these refinements. No independent validation request is made because the remaining new validation allowance is zero. Overall, this batch strengthens KEAP1 and SMARCA4 robustness in high-TMB cells, supports a clean additive PTEN contrast within KEAP1-loss cells, and suggests that PTEN is real but context-sensitive and not uniformly threshold-cleared across every stratum. Interactions remain unsupported or underpowered; no modifier effect is established. These are descriptive associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects, single-gene knockout mechanisms, or claims of external generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
H170 validation deadline: TP53-loss versus TP53-intact among MSI-negative cells with lower-quality screens. The claim direction is positive, so positive signed estimates mean higher/less negative dependency_composite, i.e. weaker composite dependency. Discovery gave signed +0.352 with 95% lower bound +0.133, while independent validation gave signed +0.583 with stringent lower bound +0.322. The validation lower bound exceeds the 0.15-unit meaningful-effect threshold, so I accept and close H170. This strengthens the TP53-loss weaker-dependency landscape in the supplied dataset and shows that it is not confined to higher-quality screens within MSI-negative cells.

Current scientific synthesis. The robust within-dataset associations are: KEAP1 loss, signed positive estimates about +0.73 to +0.93, meaning weaker composite dependency; TP53 loss, signed about +0.36 to +0.58, meaning weaker composite dependency; SMARCA4 loss, signed positive about +0.62 to +0.93 under negative-direction claims, meaning stronger composite dependency; and MSI-high status, signed about +0.74 to +0.86, meaning stronger composite dependency. These large effects persist across many contexts and several received independent validation. PTEN loss is supported as a moderate stronger-dependency association in the supplied dataset: accepted broad and contextual contrasts include point estimates roughly +0.20 to +0.38, and the narrow clean context H149 has independent validation with lower bound just clearing threshold (+0.271; lower +0.151). However, PTEN is less uniform and less precisely bounded than the large effects. Several PTEN strata remain unresolved, deferred, or threshold-sensitive, including the broader H177 context after validation failure to clear the stringent threshold, high-TMB and Cas9-quality boundaries, and some predictor contexts. Therefore PTEN should be reported as real in this dataset but context-limited and not uniformly threshold-cleared. CDKN2A is not convincingly meaningful; its point estimates cluster near or below threshold and some validation intervals are weak. Many measured predictors show no meaningful association: KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, media-serum contrast, matched-omics availability, Avana library main effect, and batch_a versus batch_b main effect. Research markers D/E/F and the three research signatures did not establish threshold-level main-effect or interaction findings under tested contrasts. Interaction claims mostly remain rejected, unresolved, or underpowered; no robust modifier or epistasis effect is established. All conclusions are descriptive associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects, single-gene knockout mechanistic claims, or externally generalizable claims. The next most informative analyses are targeted PTEN-loss contrasts, especially the registered high-Cas9/TP53-intact and low-Cas9/TP53-intact comparisons plus the newly proposed SMARCA4-intact high-Cas9 and low-Cas9 PTEN contrasts. These test whether the moderate PTEN signal survives the most relevant technical-quality and strong-predictor strata. Further tiny co-loss strata or low-information signature interactions are lower priority unless cell sizes and scientific rationale are stronger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. Validation capacity is exhausted, so these are new supplied-dataset discovery hypotheses rather than requests for independent confirmation. The signed-direction convention remains: for PTEN-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and MSI-high claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has lower, more negative dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency. For TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss claims with direction +1, a positive signed estimate means higher, less negative values, i.e. weaker composite dependency. The first four proposals refine the moderate PTEN-loss landscape by testing it in cleaner predictor and assay-quality contexts. PTEN-loss effects were attenuated or unresolved when conditioned on SMARCA4-loss and TP53-loss in earlier direct strata, so I now require both dominant contexts to be absent while also testing high versus low measured Cas9 activity and higher versus lower screen ROC quality. If these PTEN contrasts clear 0.15 signed composite units with intervals above that threshold, PTEN can be described more confidently as a real moderate within-dataset association that persists when the strongest competing predictor contexts are removed. If they remain below or imprecise around the threshold, PTEN should remain accepted only broadly or in specific validated contexts, not as uniformly robust. The last four proposals test whether the already accepted large TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and MSI-high associations persist in lower measured Cas9-activity cells. These are not mechanistic or causal claims about editing, but technical robustness checks: if the associations remain in low-Cas9 strata, they are less likely to depend only on cells with high measured Cas9 activity. If they attenuate materially, their interpretation should be qualified by assay-quality context. All proposed comparisons remain descriptive associations in the supplied dataset.

Iteration 13/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new low-Cas9 and strong-predictor-context tests mainly reinforce the dominant within-dataset landscape while sharpening the interpretation of PTEN loss as moderate and context-sensitive rather than uniformly threshold-cleared. I use the signed-direction convention: for negative-direction PTEN-loss claims, a positive signed estimate means PTEN-loss cells have lower, more negative dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency; for positive-direction TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss claims, a positive signed estimate means higher, less negative values, i.e. weaker composite dependency; for negative-direction SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger composite dependency. Several PTEN contrasts clear the 0.15-unit threshold. H204, PTEN loss among TP53-intact cells with low measured Cas9 activity, has signed estimate +0.368 with 95% lower bound +0.167, so I accept and close it. H209, PTEN loss among TP53-intact and SMARCA4-intact cells with low Cas9 activity, has signed estimate +0.396 with lower bound +0.178, and I accept and close it. H211, PTEN loss among TP53-intact and SMARCA4-intact cells in lower-quality screen-ROC strata, has signed estimate +0.403 with lower bound +0.220, so I accept this context-specific association and close that claim. These acceptances do not validate a uniform PTEN effect across all assay-quality contexts because the accepted contexts overlap and are not independent confirmations; validation capacity is exhausted. The high-Cas9 and higher-quality-screen PTEN contexts remain less clear. H205, PTEN loss with TP53 intact and high Cas9, is directionally supportive but not threshold-cleared, signed +0.248 lower bound +0.055; I leave it unresolved and active. H208, PTEN loss with TP53 and SMARCA4 intact and high Cas9, is also not threshold-cleared, signed +0.206 lower bound +0.020; I leave it unresolved and active because it is directly relevant to possible assay-quality attenuation. H206, PTEN loss with SMARCA4 intact and high Cas9, is imprecise and crosses zero, signed +0.207 lower bound -0.001; it provides little additional information, so I close its investigation while marking it unresolved. H207, PTEN loss with SMARCA4 intact and low Cas9, is near threshold but not cleared, signed +0.324 lower bound +0.108; I defer further work on that specific stratum. H210, PTEN loss among TP53- and SMARCA4-intact cells in higher-quality screen-ROC strata, remains borderline, signed +0.220 lower bound +0.106, so I leave it unresolved and active. The large accepted predictors all persist in the low-Cas9 stratum. H212 TP53 loss has signed +0.381 lower bound +0.157, just clearing threshold; I accept it but note the lower bound is marginal. H213 KEAP1 loss has signed +0.904 lower bound +0.759, H214 SMARCA4 loss has signed +0.970 lower bound +0.826, and H215 MSI-high has signed +0.872 lower bound +0.602. These are accepted and closed, but because they are tested in overlapping cells of the same supplied dataset, they are descriptive stratum evidence rather than independent replication. Multiplicity is a concern for the marginal PTEN acceptances, especially H204 and H212; however, the PTEN landscape already has multiple broader and validated accepted contrasts, and these due results are consistent with that pattern while showing attenuation or imprecision in several technical or strong-predictor contexts. Competing explanations remain: conditioning on Cas9 activity or screen-ROC quality may select cell lines with correlated unmeasured biological or technical properties, and overlapping samples mean accepted contexts are not independent. No causal inference, mechanistic single-gene-knockout claim, or external generalizability is warranted. I register two targeted interaction tests to determine whether the PTEN association is genuinely modified by lower screen quality or lower Cas9 activity within TP53- and SMARCA4-intact cells. The first claims a more negative PTEN raw contrast in lower-quality screen strata than in the complement; the second claims a more negative PTEN raw contrast in low-Cas9 strata than in the complement. These interactions use all cells in the eligible population and should be interpreted with the caveat that complements may include intermediate Cas9 or screen-quality cells because only single cutoff conditions are available. No validation request is made because no new independent validation capacity remains.

prompt:
Iteration 13/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative: Validation/response assessment: H177 asks whether PTEN loss, compared with PTEN intact, is associated with stronger composite dependency among TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative cells. Under the negative-direction convention, a positive signed estimate means PTEN-loss cells have more negative dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency. Discovery R139 gives signed estimate +0.255 with 95% lower bound +0.168, which clears the 0.15 composite-unit meaningful-effect threshold. Independent validation R145 gives signed +0.233, directionally consistent and above the threshold at the point estimate, but its stringent independent lower bound is +0.095, so it does not by itself clear the threshold. I nevertheless accept H177 and close its investigation because acceptance does not require an independently threshold-clearing validation, the supplied-dataset contrast is clearly supportive, the validation point estimate is consistent, and this claim fits a broader accepted PTEN-loss landscape. The acceptance is context-specific and should be described as moderately supported rather than as a uniformly robust, threshold-clearing validated effect across all PTEN contexts. Validation capacity is exhausted, so no new validation request is made. Scientific report: The largest and best-supported within-dataset associations are KEAP1 loss, TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status. KEAP1 loss, under direction +1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.73 to +0.93, meaning KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative dependency_composite values and therefore weaker composite dependency; independent validation for the main effect also gives signed +0.826 with lower bound +0.735. TP53 loss, under direction +1, is accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.36 to +0.58, meaning TP53-loss cells have weaker composite dependency; independent validation clears threshold in both the main contrast and the lower-screen-quality MSI-negative context, including H170 signed +0.583 with lower bound +0.322. SMARCA4 loss, under direction -1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.62 to +0.97, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger composite dependency; independent validation for main and higher-quality-screen contexts is strongly supportive. MSI-high status, under direction -1, is accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.74 to +0.87, meaning MSI-high cells have stronger composite dependency; the original positive-direction claim was correctly rejected, and the reversed H120 claim is accepted and validated. PTEN loss is supported as a moderate stronger-dependency association in the supplied dataset. Accepted PTEN-loss contexts include broad and many clean predictor contexts, with signed point estimates commonly +0.20 to +0.40, including H177 after this validation assessment. PTEN is less uniformly robust than the four large effects. Independent validation cleared the threshold in the cleanest narrow context H149 with lower bound +0.151, but in other accepted PTEN contexts validation was directionally consistent yet sometimes too imprecise to clear the threshold, as with H177. Several PTEN strata remain unresolved or threshold-sensitive, including high-Cas9 PTEN contexts, higher-screen-quality PTEN contexts, some SMARCA4-intact or TP53-intact strata, and other assay-quality or predictor-conditioned contrasts. Therefore PTEN should be reported as a real moderate association in this dataset, but context-limited and not uniformly threshold-cleared. Negative or non-meaningful findings are common among measured predictors: KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss main effect, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, MTAP loss in clean TP53-intact context, media-serum contrast, matched-omics availability, the Avana library main effect, and batch_a versus batch_b did not support threshold-level differences under tested comparisons. CDKN2A loss remains unconvincing as meaningful: its estimates are near or below threshold and validation lower bounds are weak. The constructed research markers D/E/F and the three research signatures did not produce established threshold-level main-effect or interaction findings in the analyses actually tested. Interaction evidence remains sparse and mostly not robust: no scientifically meaningful modifier or epistasis interaction has been clearly established. Some interactions are directional but imprecise, and many tiny subgroup contrasts remain underpowered. Unresolved uncertainty centers mainly on PTEN assay-quality and predictor context: registered or active claims such as H205, H208, H210, H216, and H217 remain important, especially whether lower screen quality or lower Cas9 activity strengthens the PTEN association. Additional signature, marker, and small co-loss interactions are lower priority because they are scientifically less informative and often underpowered. The next most informative analysis is to analyze the registered PTEN-loss interactions H216 and H217, along with active high-context PTEN contrasts H205, H208, and H210. These directly test whether the moderate PTEN signal is modified by technical-quality contexts after removing dominant TP53/SMARCA4 contexts. All conclusions remain descriptive associations in the supplied dataset only; they are not causal claims, single-gene knockout mechanistic claims, or evidence of external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 14/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

prompt:
Iteration 14/25, stage explore, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so these are supplied-dataset discovery proposals. The signed-direction convention remains important: for KEAP1-loss and TP53-loss claims with direction +1, a positive signed estimate means higher, less negative dependency_composite, i.e. weaker composite dependency; for SMARCA4-loss, MSI-high, and PTEN-loss claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means lower, more negative dependency_composite, i.e. stronger composite dependency. For interaction claims, the signed estimate refers to the difference between the subgroup contrast and the complement contrast; direction +1 for the PTEN high-screen attenuation test means the raw PTEN-loss contrast is expected to be less negative in higher-quality screen cells than in the complement, whereas direction -1 low-screen/low-Cas9 tests mean the raw PTEN contrast is expected to be more negative in the low-quality subgroup. I repaired the parent-linking issue by attaching available motivating result IDs whenever a new proposal is a refinement of an earlier claim. The MSI-high high-Cas9 proposal completes the assay-quality robustness check for MSI-high after the accepted low-Cas9 stratum. The KEAP1/TP53/SMARCA4 proposals test whether the already large accepted predictor effects survive jointly stringent measured assay-quality contexts: high screen ROC plus high Cas9 activity. The PTEN proposals are the main scientific focus: PTEN loss is an accepted moderate stronger-dependency association, but its magnitude is context-sensitive. I restrict to TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative cells and then examine low screen quality, high screen quality, high Cas9 activity, and low Cas9 activity, plus interactions that test whether PTEN is genuinely stronger in low screen quality or low Cas9 strata or weaker in high screen quality. If these clean contexts clear the 0.15-unit threshold, PTEN can be described more confidently as a moderate within-dataset association that persists after removing dominant predictor contexts. If they remain borderline, attenuated, or underpowered, PTEN should remain accepted broadly but not uniformly robust. All conclusions remain descriptive associations in the supplied dataset and do not imply causality, mechanistic single-gene knockout effects, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 14/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
