prompt:
Iteration 14/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Independent validation R145 gives signed +0.233, directionally consistent and above the threshold at the point estimate, but its stringent independent lower bound is +0.095, so it does not by itself clear the threshold. I nevertheless accept H177 and close its investigation because acceptance does not require an independently threshold-clearing validation, the supplied-dataset contrast is clearly supportive, the validation point estimate is consistent, and this claim fits a broader accepted PTEN-loss landscape. The acceptance is context-specific and should be described as moderately supported rather than as a uniformly robust, threshold-clearing validated effect across all PTEN contexts. Validation capacity is exhausted, so no new validation request is made. Scientific report: The largest and best-supported within-dataset associations are KEAP1 loss, TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status. KEAP1 loss, under direction +1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.73 to +0.93, meaning KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative dependency_composite values and therefore weaker composite dependency; independent validation for the main effect also gives signed +0.826 with lower bound +0.735. TP53 loss, under direction +1, is accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.36 to +0.58, meaning TP53-loss cells have weaker composite dependency; independent validation clears threshold in both the main contrast and the lower-screen-quality MSI-negative context, including H170 signed +0.583 with lower bound +0.322. SMARCA4 loss, under direction -1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.62 to +0.97, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger composite dependency; independent validation for main and higher-quality-screen contexts is strongly supportive. MSI-high status, under direction -1, is accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.74 to +0.87, meaning MSI-high cells have stronger composite dependency; the original positive-direction claim was correctly rejected, and the reversed H120 claim is accepted and validated. PTEN loss is supported as a moderate stronger-dependency association in the supplied dataset. Accepted PTEN-loss contexts include broad and many clean predictor contexts, with signed point estimates commonly +0.20 to +0.40, including H177 after this validation assessment. PTEN is less uniformly robust than the four large effects. Independent validation cleared the threshold in the cleanest narrow context H149 with lower bound +0.151, but in other accepted PTEN contexts validation was directionally consistent yet sometimes too imprecise to clear the threshold, as with H177. Several PTEN strata remain unresolved or threshold-sensitive, including high-Cas9 PTEN contexts, higher-screen-quality PTEN contexts, some SMARCA4-intact or TP53-intact strata, and other assay-quality or predictor-conditioned contrasts. Therefore PTEN should be reported as a real moderate association in this dataset, but context-limited and not uniformly threshold-cleared. Negative or non-meaningful findings are common among measured predictors: KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss main effect, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, MTAP loss in clean TP53-intact context, media-serum contrast, matched-omics availability, the Avana library main effect, and batch_a versus batch_b did not support threshold-level differences under tested comparisons. CDKN2A loss remains unconvincing as meaningful: its estimates are near or below threshold and validation lower bounds are weak. The constructed research markers D/E/F and the three research signatures did not produce established threshold-level main-effect or interaction findings in the analyses actually tested. Interaction evidence remains sparse and mostly not robust: no scientifically meaningful modifier or epistasis interaction has been clearly established. Some interactions are directional but imprecise, and many tiny subgroup contrasts remain underpowered. Unresolved uncertainty centers mainly on PTEN assay-quality and predictor context: registered or active claims such as H205, H208, H210, H216, and H217 remain important, especially whether lower screen quality or lower Cas9 activity strengthens the PTEN association. Additional signature, marker, and small co-loss interactions are lower priority because they are scientifically less informative and often underpowered. record.narrative: I assessed the newly delivered discovery results using the signed-direction convention and the 0.15 composite-unit threshold. For negative-direction PTEN-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and MSI-high claims, a positive signed estimate means more negative dependency_composite values, i.e. stronger composite dependency; for positive-direction KEAP1-loss and TP53-loss claims, a positive signed estimate means less negative values, i.e. weaker composite dependency. Several accepted contexts remain robust in the supplied dataset. H218, MSI-high status among high-Cas9 cells, gives signed +0.793 with 95% lower bound +0.548; this clears threshold comfortably and I accept it as a within-dataset context-specific stronger-dependency association, though not as independent replication. H219, KEAP1 loss among jointly high screen-ROC and high-Cas9 cells, gives signed +0.680 with lower bound +0.500; this supports weaker composite dependency in KEAP1-loss cells even in the stringent measured assay-quality context, and I accept and close it. H222, PTEN loss in the clean TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative lower-screen-quality context, gives signed +0.361 with lower bound +0.183; this is threshold-supported in that context, so I accept and close it, while emphasizing that it is one overlapping PTEN context rather than proof of uniform robustness. H220, TP53 loss in jointly high screen quality and high Cas9 activity, has signed +0.358, which is directionally supportive and above threshold at the point estimate, but its lower bound is +0.126, below the 0.15 threshold; I keep it unresolved and defer further work because broad TP53-loss effects are already accepted and this stringent stratum is less central than the PTEN assay-quality questions. The PTEN results remain informative but context-sensitive. H223, PTEN loss in the clean MSI-negative higher-screen-quality context, has signed +0.227 with lower bound +0.115; H224, PTEN loss in the clean high-Cas9 context, has signed +0.217 with lower bound +0.030; and H225, PTEN loss in the clean low-Cas9 context, has signed +0.359 with lower bound +0.142. None have interval lower bounds clearing 0.15, so I cannot accept these contexts, but they are too close and too scientifically relevant to close: I leave H223, H224, and H225 unresolved and active. They suggest possible attenuation or underprecision in higher screen-quality or high-Cas9 contexts, and possible borderline support in low-Cas9 contexts, but do not establish modification. The interaction tests do not establish effect modification. H216 and H217, broader TP53-intact/SMARCA4-intact interactions, have signed +0.193 and +0.189, respectively, but both intervals include zero and have lower bounds below zero; I leave them unresolved and deferred because the point estimates are suggestive but the uncertainty is too large. H226 and H227, the cleaner PTEN-loss interactions testing stronger raw contrasts in low screen quality or low Cas9 activity, have point estimates only +0.144 and +0.146, just below threshold, with lower bounds below zero; the evidence does not support a meaningful interaction, and I close them unresolved because further discovery on the same overlapping cells is unlikely to resolve them without independent data. H228 tests PTEN attenuation in high screen quality; its signed estimate is only +0.069 with lower bound -0.110, so there is no threshold-level evidence of attenuation. I close it unresolved rather than reject because the upper bound remains above threshold and the test is imprecise. Overall, these results strengthen accepted robustness for MSI-high, KEAP1, and one clean PTEN context, while leaving PTEN context dependence and TP53 stringent-context precision as remaining uncertainty. No independent validation capacity remains, so all conclusions are descriptive associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality, single-gene-knockout mechanism, or external generalizability.

{
  "narrative": "No assessments are due and no new voluntary validation request is available; remaining_new_requests is zero. There is also no pending validation response deadline. I nevertheless explicitly considered the STK11-loss context H18: among KEAP1-intact cells, STK11 loss is not associated with a meaningful difference in composite dependency. The signed discovery estimate was near zero, and the independent interval was signed +0.024 with lower bound -0.087 and upper bound +0.134, which is incompatible with a credibly meaningful effect. I therefore leave H18 rejected and closed.

Scientific report. The endpoint is a composite dependency score; larger negative values mean stronger dependency. Returned estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative score, i.e. stronger composite dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative score, i.e. weaker composite dependency. The meaningful-effect threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. All accepted conclusions are associations within the supplied dataset. The dataset does not establish causality, single-gene knockout mechanism, biological mechanism, or external generalizability.

The strongest and most consistently supported associations are for KEAP1 loss, TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status. KEAP1 loss, tested as direction +1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.68 to +0.93. The main effect gives signed +0.832 in discovery and +0.826 in independent validation, meaning KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative composite dependency scores and therefore weaker composite dependency. TP53 loss, tested as direction +1 after the original negative-direction claim was rejected, is accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.35 to +0.58. The main effect gives signed +0.423 in discovery and +0.356 in independent validation with lower bound +0.214, meaning TP53-loss cells have weaker composite dependency. SMARCA4 loss, tested as direction -1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.62 to +0.97. The main effect gives signed +0.833 in discovery and +0.845 in independent validation with lower bound +0.752, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger composite dependency. MSI-high status, also direction -1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.74 to +0.87. The main effect gives signed +0.792 in discovery and +0.802 in independent validation with lower bound +0.635, meaning MSI-high cells have stronger composite dependency. These four predictors represent large, well-supported within-dataset associations.

PTEN loss is supported as a moderate association but is less uniformly robust than the four large effects. The main PTEN-loss claim, direction -1, gives signed +0.227 in discovery and +0.281 in validation, meaning PTEN-loss cells tend to have stronger composite dependency. Several clean contexts are accepted, including contexts excluding TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and/or MSI-high, and several assay-quality strata. Accepted PTEN-loss contexts often have signed point estimates from about +0.20 to +0.40. However, not all PTEN contexts clear the threshold cleanly. The clean higher-screen-quality PTEN context H223 has signed +0.227 with lower bound +0.115; clean high-Cas9 PTEN context H224 has signed +0.217 with lower bound +0.030; clean low-Cas9 PTEN context H225 has signed +0.359 but lower bound +0.142. Other high-Cas9, screen-quality, or predictor-conditioned PTEN contrasts are directionally supportive but imprecise. PTEN should therefore be reported as a real moderate stronger-dependency association in this dataset, but context-sensitive and not uniformly threshold-cleared across all assay-quality and genetic contexts. The accepted PTEN contexts overlap substantially and should not be treated as independent confirmations.

The large main effects persist across many measured subgroups, including lineage subtype, screen-quality categories, Cas9-activity strata, ploidy, hypoxia, stemness, EMT, and MSI status contexts. This persistence increases confidence that the associations are not confined to one obvious subgroup. It does not establish effect modification, because persistence across overlapping subgroups is not the same evidence as a statistically meaningful interaction.

Negative or non-meaningful findings are common among other measured predictors. Main-effect differences that did not reach scientifically meaningful support include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, and MTAP loss in clean TP53-intact context. STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact cells is also rejected and validated as null. Technical or assay-context contrasts that did not support meaningful differences include media-serum contrast of 10 versus 5 percent, matched RNA/DNA omics availability, the Avana CRISPR library versus other libraries, and batch_a versus batch_b. CDKN2A loss remains unconvincing as a meaningful main effect: point estimates are near threshold in some contexts but intervals and validation are weak, so it remains unresolved rather than accepted. The constructed research markers D, E, and F and the constructed research signatures A, B, and C did not produce established threshold-level findings in the analyses actually tested.

Interaction evidence remains sparse and non-establishing. Tested interactions among major predictors, quality contexts, lineage, culture type, and constructed signatures did not support a scientifically meaningful modifier or epistasis effect. Some interactions are directional but imprecise, with intervals crossing zero and lower bounds below the 0.15 threshold; others are small and inconsistent. Thus the evidence supports main or context-stratified associations, but not robust interaction claims.

Unresolved uncertainty is centered mainly on PTEN context dependence. The registered clean PTEN contexts H223, H224, and H225 are important but do not yet provide interval-level threshold clearance in all relevant assay-quality strata. Additional active PTEN contrasts, including H205, H208, H210, H216, and H217, address similar uncertainty. TP53 precision in the most stringent combined high-screen-quality and high-Cas9 context remains slightly uncertain, although broad TP53-loss effects are already accepted. SMARCA4, KEAP1, MSI-high, and main TP53 contexts are sufficiently supported that further priority should be given to PTEN assay-quality contexts. Low-priority signature, marker, and small co-loss interaction exploration is unlikely to add informative evidence without independent validation capacity.

Next analysis. I registered one focused follow-up: a clean TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative PTEN-loss interaction in the high-Cas9-activity subgroup, direction +1, to test whether the smaller high-Cas9 PTEN point estimate represents genuine attenuation of the PTEN association relative to its complement. This directly targets the main remaining uncertainty about whether PTEN-loss effects are context-dependent in a way that matters for interpretation. I also leave the already active PTEN assay-quality contrasts available for analysis if slots allow, but overlapping discovery contrasts should not be treated as independent replication."

The signed discovery estimate was near zero, and the independent interval was signed +0.024 with lower bound -0.087 and upper bound +0.134, which is incompatible with a credibly meaningful effect. I therefore leave H18 rejected and closed.

Scientific report. The endpoint is a composite dependency score; larger negative values mean stronger dependency. Returned estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative score, i.e. stronger composite dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative score, i.e. weaker composite dependency. The meaningful-effect threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. All accepted conclusions are associations within the supplied dataset. The dataset does not establish causality, single-gene knockout mechanism, biological mechanism, or external generalizability.

The strongest and most consistently supported associations are for KEAP1 loss, TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status. KEAP1 loss, tested as direction +1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.68 to +0.93. The main effect gives signed +0.832 in discovery and +0.826 in independent validation, meaning KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative composite dependency scores and therefore weaker composite dependency. TP53 loss, tested as direction +1 after the original negative-direction claim was rejected, is accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.35 to +0.58. The main effect gives signed +0.423 in discovery and +0.356 in independent validation with lower bound +0.214, meaning TP53-loss cells have weaker composite dependency. SMARCA4 loss, tested as direction -1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.62 to +0.97. The main effect gives signed +0.833 in discovery and +0.845 in independent validation with lower bound +0.752, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger composite dependency. MSI-high status, also direction -1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.74 to +0.87. The main effect gives signed +0.792 in discovery and +0.802 in independent validation with lower bound +0.635, meaning MSI-high cells have stronger composite dependency. These four predictors represent large, well-supported within-dataset associations.

PTEN loss is supported as a moderate association but is less uniformly robust than the four large effects. The main PTEN-loss claim, direction -1, gives signed +0.227 in discovery and +0.281 in validation, meaning PTEN-loss cells tend to have stronger composite dependency. Several clean contexts are accepted, including contexts excluding TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and/or MSI-high, and several assay-quality strata. Accepted PTEN-loss contexts often have signed point estimates from about +0.20 to +0.40. However, not all PTEN contexts clear the threshold cleanly. The clean higher-screen-quality PTEN context H223 has signed +0.227 with lower bound +0.115; clean high-Cas9 PTEN context H224 has signed +0.217 with lower bound +0.030; clean low-Cas9 PTEN context H225 has signed +0.359 but lower bound +0.142. Other high-Cas9, screen-quality, or predictor-conditioned PTEN contrasts are directionally supportive but imprecise. PTEN should therefore be reported as a real moderate stronger-dependency association in this dataset, but context-sensitive and not uniformly threshold-cleared across all assay-quality and genetic contexts. The accepted PTEN contexts overlap substantially and should not be treated as independent confirmations.

The large main effects persist across many measured subgroups, including lineage subtype, screen-quality categories, Cas9-activity strata, ploidy, hypoxia, stemness, EMT, and MSI status contexts. This persistence increases confidence that the associations are not confined to one obvious subgroup. It does not establish effect modification, because persistence across overlapping subgroups is not the same evidence as a statistically meaningful interaction.

Negative or non-meaningful findings are common among other measured predictors. Main-effect differences that did not reach scientifically meaningful support include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, and MTAP loss in clean TP53-intact context. STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact cells is also rejected and validated as null. Technical or assay-context contrasts that did not support meaningful differences include media-serum contrast of 10 versus 5 percent, matched RNA/DNA omics availability, the Avana CRISPR library versus other libraries, and batch_a versus batch_b. CDKN2A loss remains unconvincing as a meaningful main effect: point estimates are near threshold in some contexts but intervals and validation are weak, so it remains unresolved rather than accepted. The constructed research markers D, E, and F and the constructed research signatures A, B, and C did not produce established threshold-level findings in the analyses actually tested.

Interaction evidence remains sparse and non-establishing. Tested interactions among major predictors, quality contexts, lineage, culture type, and constructed signatures did not support a scientifically meaningful modifier or epistasis effect. Some interactions are directional but imprecise, with intervals crossing zero and lower bounds below the 0.15 threshold; others are small and inconsistent. Thus the evidence supports main or context-stratified associations, but not robust interaction claims.

Unresolved uncertainty is centered mainly on PTEN context dependence. The registered clean PTEN contexts H223, H224, and H225 are important but do not yet provide interval-level threshold clearance in all relevant assay-quality strata. Additional active PTEN contrasts, including H205, H208, H210, H216, and H217, address similar uncertainty. TP53 precision in the most stringent combined high-screen-quality and high-Cas9 context remains slightly uncertain, although broad TP53-loss effects are already accepted. SMARCA4, KEAP1, MSI-high, and main TP53 contexts are sufficiently supported that further priority should be given to PTEN assay-quality contexts. Low-priority signature, marker, and small co-loss interaction exploration is unlikely to add informative evidence without independent validation capacity.

Next analysis. I registered one focused follow-up: a clean TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative PTEN-loss interaction in the high-Cas9-activity subgroup, direction +1, to test whether the smaller high-Cas9 PTEN point estimate represents genuine attenuation of the PTEN association relative to its complement. This directly targets the main remaining uncertainty about whether PTEN-loss effects are context-dependent in a way that matters for interpretation. I also leave the already active PTEN assay-quality contrasts available for analysis if slots allow, but overlapping discovery contrasts should not be treated as independent replication.

I therefore leave H18 rejected and closed.\n\nScientific report. The endpoint is a composite dependency score; larger negative values mean stronger dependency. Returned estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative score, i.e. stronger composite dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a less negative score, i.e. weaker composite dependency. The meaningful-effect threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. All accepted conclusions are associations within the supplied dataset. The dataset does not establish causality, single-gene knockout mechanism, biological mechanism, or external generalizability.\n\nThe strongest and most consistently supported associations are for KEAP1 loss, TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status. KEAP1 loss, tested as direction +1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.68 to +0.93. The main effect gives signed +0.832 in discovery and +0.826 in independent validation, meaning KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative composite dependency scores and therefore weaker composite dependency. TP53 loss, tested as direction +1 after the original negative-direction claim was rejected, is accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.35 to +0.58. The main effect gives signed +0.423 in discovery and +0.356 in independent validation with lower bound +0.214, meaning TP53-loss cells have weaker composite dependency. SMARCA4 loss, tested as direction -1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.62 to +0.97. The main effect gives signed +0.833 in discovery and +0.845 in independent validation with lower bound +0.752, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger composite dependency. MSI-high status, also direction -1, is repeatedly accepted with signed estimates roughly +0.74 to +0.87. The main effect gives signed +0.792 in discovery and +0.802 in independent validation with lower bound +0.635, meaning MSI-high cells have stronger composite dependency. These four predictors represent large, well-supported within-dataset associations.\n\nPTEN loss is supported as a moderate association but is less uniformly robust than the four large effects. The main PTEN-loss claim, direction -1, gives signed +0.227 in discovery and +0.281 in validation, meaning PTEN-loss cells tend to have stronger composite dependency. Several clean contexts are accepted, including contexts excluding TP53 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and/or MSI-high, and several assay-quality strata. Accepted PTEN-loss contexts often have signed point estimates from about +0.20 to +0.40. However, not all PTEN contexts clear the threshold cleanly. The clean higher-screen-quality PTEN context H223 has signed +0.227 with lower bound +0.115; clean high-Cas9 PTEN context H224 has signed +0.217 with lower bound +0.030; clean low-Cas9 PTEN context H225 has signed +0.359 but lower bound +0.142. Other high-Cas9, screen-quality, or predictor-conditioned PTEN contrasts are directionally supportive but imprecise. PTEN should therefore be reported as a real moderate stronger-dependency association in this dataset, but context-sensitive and not uniformly threshold-cleared across all assay-quality and genetic contexts. The accepted PTEN contexts overlap substantially and should not be treated as independent confirmations.\n\nThe large main effects persist across many measured subgroups, including lineage subtype, screen-quality categories, Cas9-activity strata, ploidy, hypoxia, stemness, EMT, and MSI status contexts. This persistence increases confidence that the associations are not confined to one obvious subgroup. It does not establish effect modification, because persistence across overlapping subgroups is not the same evidence as a statistically meaningful interaction.\n\nNegative or non-meaningful findings are common among other measured predictors. Main-effect differences that did not reach scientifically meaningful support include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, and MTAP loss in clean TP53-intact context. STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact cells is also rejected and validated as null. Technical or assay-context contrasts that did not support meaningful differences include media-serum contrast of 10 versus 5 percent, matched RNA/DNA omics availability, the Avana CRISPR library versus other libraries, and batch_a versus batch_b. CDKN2A loss remains unconvincing as a meaningful main effect: point estimates are near threshold in some contexts but intervals and validation are weak, so it remains unresolved rather than accepted. The constructed research markers D, E, and F and the constructed research signatures A, B, and C did not produce established threshold-level findings in the analyses actually tested.\n\nInteraction evidence remains sparse and non-establishing. Tested interactions among major predictors, quality contexts, lineage, culture type, and constructed signatures did not support a scientifically meaningful modifier or epistasis effect. Some interactions are directional but imprecise, with intervals crossing zero and lower bounds below the 0.15 threshold; others are small and inconsistent. Thus the evidence supports main or context-stratified associations, but not robust interaction claims.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty is centered mainly on PTEN context dependence. The registered clean PTEN contexts H223, H224, and H225 are important but do not yet provide interval-level threshold clearance in all relevant assay-quality strata. Additional active PTEN contrasts, including H205, H208, H210, H216, and H217, address similar uncertainty. TP53 precision in the most stringent combined high-screen-quality and high-Cas9 context remains slightly uncertain, although broad TP53-loss effects are already accepted. SMARCA4, KEAP1, MSI-high, and main TP53 contexts are sufficiently supported that further priority should be given to PTEN assay-quality contexts. Low-priority signature, marker, and small co-loss interaction exploration is unlikely to add informative evidence without independent validation capacity.\n\nNext analysis. I registered one focused follow-up: a clean TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative PTEN-loss interaction in the high-Cas9-activity subgroup, direction +1, to test whether the smaller high-Cas9 PTEN point estimate represents genuine attenuation of the PTEN association relative to its complement. record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so these are supplied-dataset discovery proposals. The main scientific uncertainty is PTEN loss: broad and many clean contexts support a moderate association between PTEN loss and stronger composite dependency, but several stringent assay-quality contexts have point estimates near or below the 0.15-unit threshold. These proposals test whether PTEN loss retains a credible threshold-supported association when major co-occurring predictors are removed and measured editing/screening quality is varied. They also ask whether PTEN effects are genuinely modified by Cas9 activity or screen quality, rather than merely varying because of co-occurrence, cell-line composition, or imprecision. The endpoint is dependency_composite; more negative values mean stronger composite dependency. For PTEN-loss and SMARCA4-loss claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means a more negative raw contrast, i.e. stronger dependency; for KEAP1-loss and TP53-loss claims with direction +1, a positive signed estimate means a less negative raw contrast, i.e. weaker dependency. For PTEN interactions, I anticipate raw attenuation in high Cas9 activity or high screen quality: the raw PTEN-loss contrast should be less negative in those high-quality strata than in their complements, so those interaction claims are direction +1 with anticipated_direction +1. For low Cas9 activity or low screen quality, I anticipate raw PTEN-loss associations to be more negative than in the complement, so those interaction claims are direction -1 with anticipated_direction -1. If high-quality attenuation interactions have intervals crossing zero or lower bounds not credibly above the signed threshold, the correct conclusion is no established effect modification, even if main effects are accepted. The KEAP1, TP53, and SMARCA4 clean high-Cas9 proposals are falsifiable persistence checks: if a major accepted predictor becomes non-threshold or implausibly attenuated after removing TP53/SMARCA4/KEAP1/PTEN/MSI contexts, it would indicate context dependence or confounding by co-occurring predictor status rather than a uniform within-dataset association. All inferences remain descriptive associations in the supplied overlapping dataset, not causal, mechanistic single-gene-knockout claims, or externally generalizable conclusions.

I selected active untested claims that directly target the main remaining scientific uncertainties: (1) whether PTEN loss retains a meaningful stronger-composite-dependency association in clean TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, KEAP1-intact, MSI-negative cells across measured Cas9-activity and screen-quality contexts, and whether these contexts represent genuine effect modification; and (2) whether the four largest accepted associations remain present after removing co-occurring major predictors. H229, H230, and H231 test PTEN loss in the clean four-predictor-removed population stratified by high Cas9, low Cas9, and low screen quality. H232-H235 test PTEN interactions with Cas9 activity and screen quality in that clean population. H236, H237, and H238 test KEAP1-loss, TP53-loss, and SMARCA4-loss effects, respectively, in the stringent high-Cas9 clean context after removing the other major predictors and MSI-high status. H196 provides a broad PTEN low-screen-quality main effect, and H221 completes the stringent assay-quality robustness check for SMARCA4 loss in jointly high screen-quality and high-Cas9 cells. Returned estimates remain signed to the claim direction. For direction -1 PTEN, SMARCA4, and MSI-high claims, positive signed estimates indicate a more negative dependency_composite and therefore stronger composite dependency. For direction +1 KEAP1 and TP53 claims, positive signed estimates indicate a less negative dependency_composite and therefore weaker composite dependency. For PTEN interaction claims, positive signed estimates indicate the claimed raw contrast shift in the named subgroup relative with the complement: H232/H234 positive signed estimates mean PTEN-loss contrasts are less negative in high Cas9 or high screen quality, i.e. attenuation; H233/H235 positive signed estimates mean PTEN-loss contrasts are more negative in low Cas9 or low screen quality. I will accept a new context or interaction only if the signed estimate and, especially, the interval lower bound credibly exceed 0.15 composite units in the claimed direction and cell counts satisfy the 20-per-cell requirement. Overlapping supplied-dataset strata are not independent replications. These analyses are descriptive associations only, not causal, mechanistic single-gene-knockout, or external generalization claims.

Iteration 15/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I assessed the signed discovery estimates with a 0.15 composite-unit threshold, accepting only when the interval lower bound credibly exceeds 0.15 in the claimed direction and all cells satisfy the n>=20 rule. For direction -1 PTEN and SMARCA4 claims, a positive signed estimate means more negative scores, i.e. stronger composite dependency; for direction +1 KEAP1 and TP53 claims, a positive signed estimate means less negative scores, i.e. weaker dependency. H230 (PTEN loss in clean low-Cas9 cells: +0.469, 95% CI +0.288 to +0.649), H231 (PTEN loss in clean low-screen-quality cells: +0.346, +0.180 to +0.512), and H196 (broad PTEN loss in low-screen-quality cells: +0.382, +0.203 to +0.560) are accepted as within-dataset context-specific stronger-dependency associations, although overlapping PTEN contexts are not independent replications. H229 (clean high-Cas9 PTEN loss: +0.235, +0.065 to +0.404) remains unresolved active: it is directionally supportive but too imprecise for threshold-level acceptance. H236 (KEAP1 loss in clean high-Cas9 cells: +0.750, +0.669 to +0.831), H238 (SMARCA4 loss in clean high-Cas9 cells: +0.826, +0.734 to +0.919), and H221 (SMARCA4 loss in jointly high-screen-quality and high-Cas9 cells: +0.691, +0.505 to +0.878) are accepted and closed; they indicate persistence of the large KEAP1 and SMARCA4 associations under stringent assay-quality contexts after removing co-occurring major predictors. Accepted PTEN-loss contexts often have signed point estimates from about +0.20 to +0.40. However, not all PTEN contexts clear the threshold cleanly. The clean higher-screen-quality PTEN context H223 has signed +0.227 with lower bound +0.115; clean high-Cas9 PTEN context H224 has signed +0.217 with lower bound +0.030; clean low-Cas9 PTEN context H225 has signed +0.359 but lower bound +0.142. Other high-Cas9, screen-quality, or predictor-conditioned PTEN contrasts are directionally supportive but imprecise. PTEN should therefore be reported as a real moderate stronger-dependency association in this dataset, but context-sensitive and not uniformly threshold-cleared across all assay-quality and genetic contexts. The accepted PTEN contexts overlap substantially and should not be treated as independent confirmations.\n\nThe large main effects persist across many measured subgroups, including lineage subtype, screen-quality categories, Cas9-activity strata, ploidy, hypoxia, stemness, EMT, and MSI status contexts. This persistence increases confidence that the associations are not confined to one obvious subgroup. It does not establish effect modification, because persistence across overlapping subgroups is not the same evidence as a statistically meaningful interaction.\n\nNegative or non-meaningful findings are common among other measured predictors. Main-effect differences that did not reach scientifically meaningful support include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, EGFR amplification, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, ERBB2 amplification, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, BRAF V600E, and MTAP loss in clean TP53-intact context. STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact cells is also rejected and validated as null. Technical or assay-context contrasts that did not support meaningful differences include media-serum contrast of 10 versus 5 percent, matched RNA/DNA omics availability, the Avana CRISPR library versus other libraries, and batch_a versus batch_b. CDKN2A loss remains unconvincing as a meaningful main effect: point estimates are near threshold in some contexts but intervals and validation are weak, so it remains unresolved rather than accepted. The constructed research markers D, E, and F and the constructed research signatures A, B, and C did not produce established threshold-level findings in the analyses actually tested.\n\nInteraction evidence remains sparse and non-establishing. Tested interactions among major predictors, quality contexts, lineage, culture type, and constructed signatures did not support a scientifically meaningful modifier or epistasis effect. Some interactions are directional but imprecise, with intervals crossing zero and lower bounds below the 0.15 threshold; others are small and inconsistent. Thus the evidence supports main or context-stratified associations, but not robust interaction claims.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty is centered mainly on PTEN context dependence. The registered clean PTEN contexts H223, H224, and H225 are important but do not yet provide interval-level threshold clearance in all relevant assay-quality strata. Additional active PTEN contrasts, including H205, H208, H210, H216, and H217, address similar uncertainty. TP53 precision in the most stringent combined high-screen-quality and high-Cas9 context remains slightly uncertain, although broad TP53-loss effects are already accepted. SMARCA4, KEAP1, MSI-high, and main TP53 contexts are sufficiently supported that further priority should be given to PTEN assay-quality contexts. Low-priority signature, marker, and small co-loss interaction exploration is unlikely to add informative evidence without independent validation capacity.\n\nNext analysis. I registered one focused follow-up: a clean TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-negative PTEN-loss interaction in the high-Cas9-activity subgroup, direction +1, to test whether the smaller high-Cas9 PTEN point estimate represents genuine attenuation of the PTEN association relative to its complement. This directly targets the main remaining uncertainty about whether PTEN-loss effects are context-dependent in a way that matters for interpretation. I also leave the already active PTEN assay-quality contrasts available for analysis if slots allow, but overlapping discovery contrasts should not be treated as independent replication."}}

record.narrative: No new independent validation was delivered and no validation response deadline is pending; independent validation capacity remains exhausted. I therefore reassessed the supplied-dataset evidence and tightened the interpretation of the accepted findings rather than changing the main accepted associations. The strongest supported within-dataset associations are unchanged: KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker composite dependency, signed +0.832 in discovery and +0.826 in independent validation; TP53 loss is associated with weaker composite dependency, signed +0.423 and +0.356; SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger composite dependency, signed +0.833 and +0.845; MSI-high is associated with stronger composite dependency, signed +0.792 and +0.802. These are large effects with validation intervals credibly above the 0.15 composite-unit threshold in the claimed direction. PTEN loss remains a moderate, real within-dataset stronger-dependency association, but its context dependence remains uncertain and several accepted PTEN contexts overlap and must not be treated as independent replications. I rejected tested interaction contrasts that failed threshold-level support: H80, H216, H217, H226, H227, H228, and H233. Together with previously rejected interactions, the evidence does not establish effect modification by Cas9 activity, screen quality, major co-predictors, lineage, culture, or constructed signatures. I closed many active untested non-PTEN and low-priority contrasts to focus remaining discovery on PTEN assay-quality contexts. The priority active set is now PTEN main effects in broad high-Cas9 cells H190, clean four-predictor high-Cas9 cells H229, clean high-screen-quality cells H223, broad high-Cas9 interaction H197, and new broad high-screen attenuation interaction H239. Negative or non-meaningful findings include main effects for KRAS, MYC, EGFR, PIK3CA, STK11, ARID1A, RB1, ERBB2, BRCA2, NF1, APC, BRAF, MTAP in clean contexts, and technical contexts such as serum level, matched RNA/DNA omics availability, Avana library, and batch_a versus batch_b. CDKN2A and the constructed research markers/signatures remain unsupported. All conclusions are descriptive associations in this dataset, not causation, single-gene knockout mechanism, biological mechanism, or external generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so these are supplied-dataset discovery proposals. The main unresolved scientific issue is whether the moderate PTEN-loss association with stronger composite dependency is robust beyond accepted broad and selected clean contexts, and whether apparent context dependence reflects true effect modification or merely imprecision/co-occurrence/composition. I propose PTEN-loss contrasts in the upper screen-quality quartile, including a broad upper-screen subgroup and a stringent TP53-intact, SMARCA4-intact, KEAP1-intact, MSI-negative upper-screen population. These test whether PTEN loss remains a threshold-supported stronger-dependency association in the highest measured screen-quality stratum rather than only in lower screen-quality or lower-quality contexts. I also propose genomic and proliferative contexts: low mutation burden, high ploidy, low growth rate, and high growth rate. These ask whether PTEN-loss effects are generalizable across genomic instability and proliferation-rate contexts, or whether the previously accepted PTEN association is concentrated in particular cell-state contexts. Finally, I propose broad PTEN-by-low-Cas9 and broad PTEN-by-upper-screen interactions. For the low-Cas9 interaction, I anticipate a more negative raw PTEN contrast in the low-Cas9 subgroup than in its complement, suggesting low-Cas9 strengthening. For the upper-screen attenuation interaction, I anticipate a less negative raw PTEN contrast in the upper-screen subgroup than in its complement, suggesting high screen-quality attenuation. For main PTEN-loss claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, i.e. stronger composite dependency. For the upper-screen attenuation interaction with direction +1, a positive signed estimate means the raw interaction is positive, i.e. attenuation. For the low-Cas9 interaction with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the raw interaction is negative, i.e. strengthening in the low-Cas9 subgroup. In every case, a claim is meaningful only if the signed estimate and preferably the signed lower bound exceed +0.15 composite units in the claimed direction, with all cells satisfying the n>=20 rule. If the main upper-screen contrast is threshold-supported but the upper-screen interaction is not, that supports a robust main association without established screen-quality effect modification. If the clean upper-screen main contrast falls below threshold, that would indicate context dependence, co-predictor confounding, selection/composition effects, or insufficient power rather than proof of absence. All comparisons are descriptive associations within the supplied dataset and overlapping strata are not independent replications; no causal, single-gene-knockout mechanistic, or external generalization claims are implied.

prompt:
Iteration 16/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this analysis request focuses on untested supplied-dataset discovery contrasts. I selected eight active PTEN claims: H239 broad PTEN-by-low-screen interaction, H241 PTEN loss in clean upper-quartile screen-quality cells, H242 PTEN loss in low mutation burden, H243 PTEN loss in high ploidy, H244 PTEN loss in low growth rate, H245 PTEN loss in high growth rate, H246 broad PTEN-by-low-Cas9 interaction, and H247 broad PTEN-by-upper-quartile-screen attenuation interaction. These test whether the moderate PTEN-loss stronger-dependency association is retained across measured assay-quality, genomic instability, and proliferation contexts, and whether apparent context dependence reflects effect modification. I omitted H240 because it duplicates the already accepted broad low-screen PTEN main contrast in H196, and I closed duplicate H197 because H246 is the same broad low-Cas9 interaction. H223, H229, and H190 already have discovery evidence and were not rerun because they would reuse the same data rather than provide new sample. For direction -1 main PTEN claims, positive signed estimates indicate stronger composite dependency. For direction -1 interactions, positive signed estimates indicate strengthening of the PTEN contrast in the named subgroup. For H247 direction +1, positive signed estimates indicate attenuation in the upper-screen subgroup. Acceptance requires the signed estimate and preferably the interval lower bound to credibly exceed 0.15 composite units in the claimed direction, with all comparison cells satisfying n>=20. Overlapping contexts are not independent replications, and all claims remain descriptive associations within the supplied dataset, not causality, single-gene-knockout mechanism, or generalizability.
